AWSTemplateFormatVersion: "2010-09-09"
Description: >-
  AWS Backup Audit Manager framework implementing backup compliance with the
  five default controls, including minimum recovery point retention of 35 days
  and a minimum backup plan frequency of 24 hours with 35 day retention.
  AWS Config is enabled in this template because Backup Audit Manager deploys
  and evaluates its controls as AWS Config rules.

Resources:
  ConfigBucketKey:
    Type: AWS::KMS::Key
    Properties:
      Description: Customer managed key that encrypts the AWS Config delivery bucket.
      EnableKeyRotation: true
      KeyPolicy:
        Version: "2012-10-17"
        Statement:
          - Sid: EnableIamPolicies
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              AWS: !Sub arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::${AWS::AccountId}:root
            Action: "kms:*"
            Resource: "*"

  ConfigBucket:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
    Properties:
      BucketEncryption:
        ServerSideEncryptionConfiguration:
          - ServerSideEncryptionByDefault:
              SSEAlgorithm: aws:kms
              KMSMasterKeyID: !GetAtt ConfigBucketKey.Arn
            BucketKeyEnabled: true
      OwnershipControls:
        Rules:
          - ObjectOwnership: BucketOwnerEnforced
      PublicAccessBlockConfiguration:
        BlockPublicAcls: true
        BlockPublicPolicy: true
        IgnorePublicAcls: true
        RestrictPublicBuckets: true
      VersioningConfiguration:
        Status: Enabled

  ConfigBucketPolicy:
    Type: AWS::S3::BucketPolicy
    Properties:
      Bucket: !Ref ConfigBucket
      PolicyDocument:
        Version: "2012-10-17"
        Statement:
          - Sid: AWSConfigBucketPermissionsCheck
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: config.amazonaws.com
            Action: s3:GetBucketAcl
            Resource: !GetAtt ConfigBucket.Arn
          - Sid: AWSConfigBucketDelivery
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: config.amazonaws.com
            Action: s3:PutObject
            Resource: !Sub "${ConfigBucket.Arn}/*"
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                s3:x-amz-acl: bucket-owner-full-control
          - Sid: DenyInsecureTransport
            Effect: Deny
            Principal: "*"
            Action: "s3:*"
            Resource:
              - !GetAtt ConfigBucket.Arn
              - !Sub "${ConfigBucket.Arn}/*"
            Condition:
              Bool:
                aws:SecureTransport: "false"

  ConfigRecorderRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      Description: >-
        Allows AWS Config to record resource configuration and deliver
        snapshots for the AWS Backup Audit Manager framework controls.
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: "2012-10-17"
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: config.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - !Sub arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AWS_ConfigRole
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: ConfigBucketKeyAccess
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: "2012-10-17"
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - kms:Decrypt
                  - kms:GenerateDataKey
                Resource: !GetAtt ConfigBucketKey.Arn

  ConfigDeliveryChannel:
    Type: AWS::Config::DeliveryChannel
    DependsOn: ConfigBucketPolicy
    Properties:
      S3BucketName: !Ref ConfigBucket
      ConfigSnapshotDeliveryProperties:
        DeliveryFrequency: TwentyFour_Hours

  ConfigRecorder:
    Type: AWS::Config::ConfigurationRecorder
    Properties:
      Name: default
      RoleARN: !GetAtt ConfigRecorderRole.Arn
      RecordingGroup:
        AllSupported: true

  BackupComplianceFramework:
    Type: AWS::Backup::Framework
    DependsOn: ConfigRecorder
    Properties:
      FrameworkName: BackupComplianceFramework
      FrameworkDescription: >-
        Backup compliance framework enforcing encrypted, immutable and retained
        recovery points along with a minimum backup frequency and retention.
      FrameworkControls:
        - ControlName: BACKUP_RESOURCES_PROTECTED_BY_BACKUP_PLAN
        - ControlName: BACKUP_RECOVERY_POINT_ENCRYPTED
        - ControlName: BACKUP_RECOVERY_POINT_MANUAL_DELETION_DISABLED
        - ControlName: BACKUP_RECOVERY_POINT_MINIMUM_RETENTION_CHECK
          ControlInputParameters:
            - ParameterName: requiredRetentionDays
              ParameterValue: "35"
        - ControlName: BACKUP_PLAN_MIN_FREQUENCY_AND_MIN_RETENTION_CHECK
          ControlInputParameters:
            - ParameterName: requiredFrequencyUnit
              ParameterValue: hours
            - ParameterName: requiredFrequencyValue
              ParameterValue: "24"
            - ParameterName: requiredRetentionDays
              ParameterValue: "35"
      FrameworkTags:
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: iac-god-eval

Outputs:
  FrameworkArn:
    Description: ARN of the AWS Backup Audit Manager framework.
    Value: !GetAtt BackupComplianceFramework.FrameworkArn
  FrameworkCreationTime:
    Description: Creation time of the framework.
    Value: !GetAtt BackupComplianceFramework.CreationTime
  FrameworkStatus:
    Description: Deployment status of the framework.
    Value: !GetAtt BackupComplianceFramework.DeploymentStatus
  ConfigBucketName:
    Description: Name of the S3 bucket used by AWS Config.
    Value: !Ref ConfigBucket

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: 'Provisions a Lightsail instance with an attached disk for testing.'

Parameters:
  BlueprintId:
    Type: String
    Description: Blueprint for the Lightsail instance (Amazon Linux 2023).
    Default: amazon_linux_2023
  BundleId:
    Type: String
    Description: Bundle (instance plan) for the Lightsail instance (nano).
    Default: nano_3_0
  AvailabilityZone:
    Type: String
    Description: The first available availability zone for the resources.
    Default: us-east-1a
  DiskSizeInGb:
    Type: Number
    Description: Size of the attached disk in GB.
    Default: 8

Resources:
  MyLightsailInstance:
    Type: AWS::Lightsail::Instance
    Properties:
      BlueprintId: !Ref BlueprintId
      BundleId: !Ref BundleId
      InstanceName: !Ref 'AWS::StackName'
      AvailabilityZone: !Ref AvailabilityZone
      Tags:
        - Key: tutorial
          Value: !Ref 'AWS::StackName'

  MyLightsailDisk:
    Type: AWS::Lightsail::Disk
    Properties:
      DiskName: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-disk'
      SizeInGb: !Ref DiskSizeInGb
      AvailabilityZone: !Ref AvailabilityZone
      Tags:
        - Key: tutorial
          Value: !Ref 'AWS::StackName'

  # CloudFormation cannot attach a Lightsail disk natively (the AttachedTo
  # property on AWS::Lightsail::Disk is read-only and the provider never issues
  # AttachDisk). A small custom resource performs the attachment.
  DiskAttachmentRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: lambda.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: DiskAttachmentPolicy
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - lightsail:AttachDisk
                  - lightsail:DetachDisk
                  - lightsail:GetDisk
                  - lightsail:GetInstance
                Resource:
                  - !GetAtt MyLightsailDisk.DiskArn
                  - !GetAtt MyLightsailInstance.InstanceArn
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - logs:CreateLogGroup
                  - logs:CreateLogStream
                  - logs:PutLogEvents
                Resource:
                  - !Sub 'arn:aws:logs:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:log-group:/aws/lambda/*:*'

  DiskAttachmentFunction:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    Properties:
      Handler: index.handler
      Role: !GetAtt DiskAttachmentRole.Arn
      Runtime: python3.12
      Timeout: 600
      Code:
        ZipFile: |
          import boto3
          import time
          import cfnresponse

          def _wait_ready(instance_name, disk_name, timeout=400):
              client = boto3.client('lightsail')
              deadline = time.time() + timeout
              while time.time() < deadline:
                  running = False
                  available = False
                  try:
                      inst = client.get_instance(instanceName=instance_name)['instance']
                      running = inst.get('state', {}).get('name') == 'running'
                  except Exception:
                      pass
                  try:
                      d = client.get_disk(diskName=disk_name)['disk']
                      available = d.get('state') == 'available'
                  except Exception:
                      pass
                  if running and available:
                      return True
                  time.sleep(8)
              return False

          def handler(event, context):
              props = event.get('ResourceProperties', {})
              disk = props.get('DiskName')
              inst = props.get('InstanceName')
              rt = event.get('RequestType', 'Create')
              data = {}
              status = cfnresponse.FAILED
              msg = rt + ' request failed'
              try:
                  client = boto3.client('lightsail')
                  if rt in ('Create', 'Update'):
                      _wait_ready(inst, disk)
                      client.attach_disk(diskName=disk, instanceName=inst, diskPath='/dev/xvdf')
                      data['Attached'] = True
                      msg = 'attached disk ' + str(disk)
                  elif rt == 'Delete':
                      try:
                          client.detach_disk(diskName=disk)
                      except Exception:
                          pass
                      data['Detached'] = True
                      msg = 'detached disk ' + str(disk)
                  status = cfnresponse.SUCCESS
              except Exception as e:
                  msg = msg + ': ' + str(e)
                  data['Error'] = str(e)
              cfnresponse.send(event, context, status, data,
                               physicalResourceId=(str(inst) + '-' + str(disk)))
              return

  DiskAttachmentPermission:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Permission
    Properties:
      Action: lambda:InvokeFunction
      FunctionName: !Ref DiskAttachmentFunction
      Principal: cloudformation.amazonaws.com
      SourceArn: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:cloudformation:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:stack/${AWS::StackName}/*'

  DiskAttachment:
    Type: AWS::CloudFormation::CustomResource
    Properties:
      ServiceToken: !GetAtt DiskAttachmentFunction.Arn
      DiskName: !Ref MyLightsailDisk
      InstanceName: !Ref MyLightsailInstance

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: >
  Serverless workflow using Step Functions that sends custom events to a custom
  EventBridge event bus, with a rule forwarding all events to CloudWatch Logs.

Parameters:
  LogGroupRetentionDays:
    Type: Number
    Default: 7
    Description: Number of days to retain log events in CloudWatch Logs.
    AllowedValues:
      - 1
      - 3
      - 7
      - 14
      - 30
      - 60
      - 90
      - 120
      - 150
      - 180
      - 365
      - 400
      - 545
      - 731
      - 1827
      - 3653

Resources:
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Custom EventBridge Event Bus
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  CustomEventBus:
    Type: AWS::Events::EventBus
    Properties:
      Name: CustomWorkflowBus

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # CloudWatch Logs Log Group for capturing all events from the custom bus
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  LogGroup:
    Type: AWS::Logs::LogGroup
    Properties:
      LogGroupName: /aws/events/custom-workflow-bus
      RetentionInDays: !Ref LogGroupRetentionDays

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Resource policy on the log group allowing EventBridge to write events
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  LogGroupResourcePolicy:
    Type: AWS::Logs::ResourcePolicy
    Properties:
      PolicyName: EventBridgeWriteToLogGroup
      PolicyDocument:
        Fn::Sub:
          - |-
            {
              "Version": "2012-10-17",
              "Statement": [
                {
                  "Effect": "Allow",
                  "Principal": {
                    "Service": "events.amazonaws.com"
                  },
                  "Action": [
                    "logs:CreateLogStream",
                    "logs:PutLogEvents"
                  ],
                  "Resource": "${LogGroupArn}"
                }
              ]
            }
          - LogGroupArn: !GetAtt LogGroup.Arn

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # EventBridge Rule on the custom bus that forwards ALL events to CloudWatch
  # Logs for testing and debugging
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  EventBridgeRule:
    Type: AWS::Events::Rule
    Properties:
      EventBusName: !Ref CustomEventBus
      Name: ForwardAllToCloudWatchLogs
      Description: Forwards every event on the custom bus to CloudWatch Logs.
      EventPattern:
        source:
          - prefix: ""
      State: ENABLED
      Targets:
        - Arn: !GetAtt LogGroup.Arn
          Id: CloudWatchLogsTarget

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # IAM role for the Step Functions state machine
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  StateMachineRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service:
                - states.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: PutEventsOnCustomBus
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action: events:PutEvents
                Resource: !GetAtt CustomEventBus.Arn

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Step Functions state machine that sends custom events to the event bus
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  StateMachine:
    Type: AWS::StepFunctions::StateMachine
    Properties:
      StateMachineName: EventPublishWorkflow
      StateMachineType: STANDARD
      RoleArn: !GetAtt StateMachineRole.Arn
      DefinitionString:
        Fn::Sub:
          - |-
            {
              "StartAt": "SendEvent",
              "States": {
                "SendEvent": {
                  "Type": "Task",
                  "Resource": "arn:aws:states:::events:putEvents",
                  "Parameters": {
                    "Entries": [
                      {
                        "EventBusName": "${EventBusName}",
                        "Source": "custom.workflow",
                        "DetailType": "WorkflowEvent",
                        "Detail": {
                          "message": "Hello from Step Functions workflow"
                        }
                      }
                    ]
                  },
                  "End": true
                }
              }
            }
          - EventBusName: !Ref CustomEventBus

Outputs:

  CustomEventBusArn:
    Description: ARN of the custom EventBridge event bus

  LogGroupName:
    Description: Name of the CloudWatch Logs log group
    Value: !Ref LogGroup
  StateMachineArn:
    Description: ARN of the Step Functions state machine
    Value: !Ref StateMachine

Description: >-
  Serverless workflow that monitors EC2 instance state changes on the default
  event bus and triggers a Step Functions state machine whenever an instance
  transitions to running, stopped, or terminated. Each transition path includes
  a placeholder state for future business logic.

Parameters: {}

Resources:
  InstanceStateChangeLogGroup:
    Type: AWS::Logs::LogGroup
    Properties:
      LogGroupName: /aws/vendedlogs/states/ec2-instance-state-change-workflow
      RetentionInDays: 30

  InstanceStateMachineRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: "2012-10-17"
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: states.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: CloudWatchLogsDeliveryAndWrite
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: "2012-10-17"
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - logs:CreateLogDelivery
                  - logs:GetLogDelivery
                  - logs:UpdateLogDelivery
                  - logs:DeleteLogDelivery
                  - logs:ListLogDeliveries
                  - logs:PutResourcePolicy
                  - logs:DescribeResourcePolicies
                  - logs:DescribeLogGroups
                Resource: "*"
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - logs:CreateLogStream
                  - logs:PutLogEvents
                Resource: !Sub "${InstanceStateChangeLogGroup.Arn}:*"

  EC2InstanceStateChangeWorkflow:
    Type: AWS::StepFunctions::StateMachine
    Properties:
      StateMachineName: ec2-instance-state-change-workflow
      RoleArn: !GetAtt InstanceStateMachineRole.Arn
      DefinitionString: |
        {
          "Comment": "EC2 Instance State Change Workflow",
          "StartAt": "Route on State Change",
          "States": {
            "Route on State Change": {
              "Type": "Choice",
              "Choices": [
                {
                  "Variable": "$.detail.state",
                  "StringEquals": "running",
                  "Next": "Running Path Business Logic"
                },
                {
                  "Variable": "$.detail.state",
                  "StringEquals": "stopped",
                  "Next": "Stopped Path Business Logic"
                },
                {
                  "Variable": "$.detail.state",
                  "StringEquals": "terminated",
                  "Next": "Terminated Path Business Logic"
                }
              ],
              "Default": "Workflow Complete"
            },
            "Running Path Business Logic": {
              "Type": "Pass",
              "Comment": "Placeholder for business logic to execute when an instance enters the running state.",
              "Next": "Workflow Complete"
            },
            "Stopped Path Business Logic": {
              "Type": "Pass",
              "Comment": "Placeholder for business logic to execute when an instance enters the stopped state.",
              "Next": "Workflow Complete"
            },
            "Terminated Path Business Logic": {
              "Type": "Pass",
              "Comment": "Placeholder for business logic to execute when an instance enters the terminated state.",
              "Next": "Workflow Complete"
            },
            "Workflow Complete": {
              "Type": "Succeed"
            }
          }
        }
      LoggingConfiguration:
        Level: ALL
        IncludeExecutionData: false
        Destinations:
          - CloudWatchLogsLogGroup:
              LogGroupArn: !GetAtt InstanceStateChangeLogGroup.Arn

  EventBridgeInvokeRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: "2012-10-17"
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: events.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: StartStepFunctionsExecution
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: "2012-10-17"
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action: states:StartExecution
                Resource: !GetAtt EC2InstanceStateChangeWorkflow.Arn

  EC2InstanceStateChangeRule:
    Type: AWS::Events::Rule
    Properties:
      Name: ec2-instance-state-change-workflow-rule
      EventBusName: default
      EventPattern:
        source:
          - aws.ec2
        detail-type:
          - EC2 Instance State-change Notification
        detail:

      Timeout: 120
      Code:
        ZipFile: |
          import json
          import urllib.request

          import boto3

          SCHEMAS = boto3.client("schemas")


          def send_response(event, context, status, data=None, physical_resource_id=None, reason=None):
              response_body = {
                  "Status": status,
                  "Reason": reason or "See the details in CloudWatch Log Stream: " + context.log_stream_name,
                  "PhysicalResourceId": physical_resource_id or context.log_stream_name,
                  "StackId": event["StackId"],
                  "RequestId": event["RequestId"],
                  "LogicalResourceId": event["LogicalResourceId"],
                  "NoEcho": False,
                  "Data": data or {},
              }
              json_body = json.dumps(response_body)
              request = urllib.request.Request(
                  event["ResponseURL"],
                  data=json_body.encode("utf-8"),
                  headers={"Content-Length": str(len(json_body))},
                  method="PUT",
              )
              with urllib.request.urlopen(request) as response:
                  return response.status


          def create_discoverer(source_arn):
              response = SCHEMAS.create_discoverer(
                  SourceArn=source_arn,
                  Description="Schema discoverer for the retail demo store event bus",
              )
              return response["DiscovererArn"], response["DiscovererId"]


          def find_existing(source_arn):
              paginator = SCHEMAS.get_paginator("list_discoverers")
              for page in paginator.paginate():
                  for discoverer in page.get("Discoverers", []):
                      if discoverer.get("SourceArn") == source_arn:
                          return discoverer["DiscovererArn"], discoverer["DiscovererId"]
              return None


          def ensure_discoverer(source_arn, existing_id=None):
              if existing_id:
                  try:
                      response = SCHEMAS.describe_discoverer(DiscovererId=existing_id)
                      return response["DiscovererArn"], response["DiscovererId"]
                  except SCHEMAS.exceptions.NotFoundException:
                      pass
              try:
                  return create_discoverer(source_arn)
              except SCHEMAS.exceptions.ConflictException:
                  existing = find_existing(source_arn)
                  if existing:
                      return existing
                  return create_discoverer(source_arn)


          def delete_discoverer(discoverer_id):
              if not discoverer_id:
                  return
              try:
                  SCHEMAS.delete_discoverer(DiscovererId=discoverer_id)
              except Exception:
                  # The discoverer may already be gone or the id may not
                  # reference an actual discoverer (e.g. after a failed create);
                  # deletion of a non-existent discoverer is a no-op.
                  pass


          def handler(event, context):
              request_type = event["RequestType"]
              props = event.get("ResourceProperties", {})
              source_arn = props.get("SourceArn")
              physical_resource_id = event.get("PhysicalResourceId")
              data = {}
              try:
                  if request_type == "Create":
                      arn, discoverer_id = ensure_discoverer(source_arn)
                      physical_resource_id = discoverer_id
                      data = {"DiscovererArn": arn, "DiscovererId": discoverer_id}
                  elif request_type == "Update":
                      old_props = event.get("OldResourceProperties", {})
                      if old_props.get("SourceArn") != source_arn:
                          delete_discoverer(physical_resource_id)
                          arn, discoverer_id = ensure_discoverer(source_arn)
                      else:
                          arn, discoverer_id = ensure_discoverer(source_arn, physical_resource_id)
                      physical_resource_id = discoverer_id
                      data = {"DiscovererArn": arn, "DiscovererId": discoverer_id}
                  elif request_type == "Delete":
                      delete_discoverer(physical_resource_id)
                  send_response(event, context, "SUCCESS", data, physical_resource_id)
              except Exception as exception:
                  send_response(event, context, "FAILED", {}, physical_resource_id, str(exception))

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: "2010-09-09"

Description: >-
  Idempotency store for a hybrid mode deduplication scenario in which polling-
  and event-driven workflows may trigger duplicate executions for the same file.
  Backed by DynamoDB with a composite primary key (partition key + sort key),
  Time-to-Live (default 7 days), Point-in-Time Recovery (enabled by default),
  and a managed IAM policy granting Lambda and Step Functions read/write access
  to the table.

Parameters:
  ProjectPrefix:
    Type: String
    Default: fsxn-s3ap
    Description: >-
      Prefix used when naming the resources created by this stack (the DynamoDB
      table and the IAM managed policy).
    AllowedPattern: "^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9])?$"
    MinLength: "1"
    MaxLength: "63"
    ConstraintDescription: >-
      ProjectPrefix must be 1-63 characters, lowercase letters, digits, or
      hyphens, and must start and end with an alphanumeric character.

  IdempotencyKeyAttribute:
    Type: String
    Default: idempotency_key
    Description: >-
      Name of the composite partition (HASH) key storing the deduplication key
      (for example, a hash of the file path plus the operation scope).
    MinLength: "1"
    MaxLength: "255"

  SortKeyAttribute:
    Type: String
    Default: sort_key
    Description: >-
      Name of the composite sort (RANGE) key, used to group duplicate
      executions that share the same partition key (for example, the event
      source or workflow name).
    MinLength: "1"
    MaxLength: "255"

  TTLAttribute:
    Type: String
    Default: expiry
    Description: >-
      Name of the DynamoDB Time-to-Live attribute. Items must store a UNIX
      epoch time in seconds as a number for DynamoDB to expire them.
    MinLength: "1"
    MaxLength: "255"

  TTLDurationDays:
    Type: Number
    Default: 7
    MinValue: 1
    MaxValue: 3650
    Description: >-
      Default Time-to-Live duration in days applied to items written into the
      table (defaults to 7). Producers should set the TTL attribute to
      current UNIX epoch seconds + TTLDurationDays * 86400.

  EnablePITR:
    Type: String
    Default: "true"
    AllowedValues:
      - "true"
      - "false"
    Description: >-
      Enables Point-in-Time Recovery (continuous backups) on the idempotency
      table. Enabled by default.

Conditions:
  IsPITREnabled: !Equals [!Ref EnablePITR, "true"]

Resources:
  IdempotencyStoreTable:
    Type: AWS::DynamoDB::Table
    Properties:
      TableName: !Sub "${ProjectPrefix}-idempotency-store"
      AttributeDefinitions:
        - AttributeName: !Ref IdempotencyKeyAttribute
          AttributeType: S
        - AttributeName: !Ref SortKeyAttribute
          AttributeType: S
      KeySchema:
        - AttributeName: !Ref IdempotencyKeyAttribute
          KeyType: HASH
        - AttributeName: !Ref SortKeyAttribute
          KeyType: RANGE
      BillingMode: PAY_PER_REQUEST
      DeletionProtectionEnabled: false
      SSESpecification:
        SSEEnabled: true
      TimeToLiveSpecification:
        AttributeName: !Ref TTLAttribute
        Enabled: true
      PointInTimeRecoverySpecification:
        PointInTimeRecoveryEnabled: !If [IsPITREnabled, true, false]

  IdempotencyStoreAccessPolicy:
    Type: AWS::IAM::ManagedPolicy
    Properties:
      ManagedPolicyName: !Sub "${ProjectPrefix}-idempotency-store-policy"
      Description: >-
        Managed policy granting Lambda and Step Functions execution roles
        read/write access to the DynamoDB idempotency store table.
      PolicyDocument:
        Version: "2012-10-17"
        Statement:
          - Sid: IdempotencyStoreDataPlaneAccess
            Effect: Allow
            Action:
              - dynamodb:GetItem
              - dynamodb:PutItem
              - dynamodb:UpdateItem
              - dynamodb:DeleteItem
              - dynamodb:Query
              - dynamodb:Scan
              - dynamodb:BatchGetItem
              - dynamodb:BatchWriteItem
              - dynamodb:ConditionCheckItem
              - dynamodb:DescribeTable
            Resource:
              - !GetAtt IdempotencyStoreTable.Arn
              - !Sub "${IdempotencyStoreTable.Arn}/index/*"

Outputs:
  IdempotencyStoreTableName:
    Description: Name of the DynamoDB idempotency store table.
    Value: !Ref IdempotencyStoreTable
  IdempotencyStoreTableArn:
    Description: ARN of the DynamoDB idempotency store table.
    Value: !GetAtt IdempotencyStoreTable.Arn
  IdempotencyStoreAccessPolicyArn:
    Description: >-
      ARN of the managed IAM policy to attach to Lambda and Step Functions
      execution roles for read/write access to the idempotency store.
    Value: !Ref IdempotencyStoreAccessPolicy
  TTLAttributeName:
    Description: >-
      Name of the Time-to-Live attribute; values must be UNIX epoch seconds.
    Value: !Ref TTLAttribute
  TTLDurationDays:
    Description: >-
      Default Time-to-Live duration in days used by producers of items.
    Value: !Ref TTLDurationDays

final_template:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: >
  Chaos engineering workflow using AWS Step Functions to test the resilience of
  an ECS service. The state machine terminates a specific EC2 instance, waits
  300 seconds, checks the health of an ECS service, and publishes an SNS alert
  if the service is unhealthy. All resources (VPC, EC2 instance, ECS cluster and
  service, SNS topic, Lambda functions, IAM roles, and the state machine) are
  created inside this template.

Resources:
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Networking
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  ChaosVpc:
    Type: AWS::EC2::VPC
    Properties:
      CidrBlock: 10.0.0.0/16
      EnableDnsSupport: true
      EnableDnsHostnames: true
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: chaos-vpc

  InternetGateway:
    Type: AWS::EC2::InternetGateway
    Properties:
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: chaos-igw

  InternetGatewayAttachment:
    Type: AWS::EC2::VPCGatewayAttachment
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref ChaosVpc
      InternetGatewayId: !Ref InternetGateway

  PublicSubnet:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Subnet
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref ChaosVpc
      CidrBlock: 10.0.0.0/24
      AvailabilityZone: !Select [0, !GetAZs '']
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: chaos-public-subnet

  PublicRouteTable:
    Type: AWS::EC2::RouteTable
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref ChaosVpc
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: chaos-route-table

  PublicRoute:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Route
    DependsOn: InternetGatewayAttachment
    Properties:
      RouteTableId: !Ref PublicRouteTable
      DestinationCidrBlock: 0.0.0.0/0
      GatewayId: !Ref InternetGateway

  PublicSubnetRouteTableAssociation:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SubnetRouteTableAssociation
    Properties:
      SubnetId: !Ref PublicSubnet
      RouteTableId: !Ref PublicRouteTable

  ChaosTargetSecurityGroup:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: Security group for the chaos engineering target EC2 instance
      VpcId: !Ref ChaosVpc
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: chaos-target-sg

  EcsServiceSecurityGroup:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: Security group for the ECS Fargate service tasks
      VpcId: !Ref ChaosVpc
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: chaos-ecs-sg

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Chaos target EC2 instance (AMI is resolved dynamically, no hardcoded AMI)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  ChaosEbsKey:
    Type: AWS::KMS::Key
    Properties:
      Description: Customer managed KMS key used to encrypt the chaos target EC2 instance root volume
      EnableKeyRotation: true
      PendingWindowInDays: 7
      KeyPolicy:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: Enable root access
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              AWS: !Sub arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::${AWS::AccountId}:root
            Action: kms:*
            Resource: '*'

  ChaosEbsKeyAlias:
    Type: AWS::KMS::Alias
    Properties:
      AliasName: alias/chaos-ebs-key
      TargetKeyId: !Ref ChaosEbsKey

  ChaosInstance:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Instance
    Properties:
      ImageId: !GetAtt AmiLookup.ImageId
      InstanceType: t3.micro
      SubnetId: !Ref PublicSubnet
      SecurityGroupIds:
        - !Ref ChaosTargetSecurityGroup
      BlockDeviceMappings:
        - DeviceName: /dev/xvda
          Ebs:
            VolumeSize: 8
            VolumeType: gp2
            Encrypted: true
            KmsKeyId: !GetAtt ChaosEbsKey.Arn
      MetadataOptions:
        HttpTokens: required
        HttpEndpoint: enabled
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: chaos-target-instance

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # ECS cluster, task definition, and service
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  ChaosCluster:
    Type: AWS::ECS::Cluster
    Properties:
      ClusterName: chaos-cluster
      ClusterSettings:
        - Name: containerInsights
          Value: enabled
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: chaos-cluster

  EcsTaskLogGroup:
    Type: AWS::Logs::LogGroup
    Properties:
      LogGroupName: /ecs/chaos-ecs-service
      RetentionInDays: 14

  EcsTaskExecutionRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: ecs-tasks.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: EcsTaskExecutionPolicy
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - logs:CreateLogGroup
                Resource: '*'
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - logs:CreateLogStream
                  - logs:PutLogEvents
                Resource:
                  - !Sub arn:${AWS::Partition}:logs:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:log-group:/ecs/chaos-ecs-service:*
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - ecr:GetDownloadUrlForLayer
                  - ecr:BatchGetImage
                  - ecr:BatchCheckLayerAvailability
                  - ecr:GetAuthorizationToken
                Resource: '*'

  ChaosTaskDefinition:
    Type: AWS::ECS::TaskDefinition
    Properties:
      Family: chaos-ecs-task
      RequiresCompatibilities:
        - FARGATE
      NetworkMode: awsvpc
      Cpu: '256'
      Memory: '512'
      ExecutionRoleArn: !GetAtt EcsTaskExecutionRole.Arn
      ContainerDefinitions:
        - Name: chaos-ecs-container
          Image: public.ecr.aws/docker/library/nginx:latest
          Essential: true
          PortMappings:
            - ContainerPort: 80
              Protocol: tcp
          LogConfiguration:
            LogDriver: awslogs
            Options:
              awslogs-group: /ecs/chaos-ecs-service
              awslogs-region: !Ref AWS::Region
              awslogs-stream-prefix: chaos

  ChaosEcsService:
    Type: AWS::ECS::Service
    Properties:
      Cluster: !Ref ChaosCluster
      ServiceName: chaos-ecs-service
      TaskDefinition: !Ref ChaosTaskDefinition
      DesiredCount: 1
      LaunchType: FARGATE
      PlatformVersion: LATEST
      NetworkConfiguration:
        AwsvpcConfiguration:
          Subnets:
            - !Ref PublicSubnet
          SecurityGroups:
            - !Ref EcsServiceSecurityGroup
          AssignPublicIp: ENABLED
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: chaos-ecs-service

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # SNS alert topic (encrypted with a customer managed KMS key)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  AlertTopicKey:
    Type: AWS::KMS::Key
    Properties:
      Description: Customer managed KMS key used to encrypt the chaos alert SNS topic
      EnableKeyRotation: true
      PendingWindowInDays: 7
      KeyPolicy:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: Enable root access
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              AWS: !Sub arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::${AWS::AccountId}:root
            Action: kms:*
            Resource: '*'
          - Sid: Allow SNS service to use the key
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: sns.amazonaws.com
            Action:
              - kms:Decrypt
              - kms:GenerateDataKey
            Resource: '*'

  AlertTopicKeyAlias:
    Type: AWS::KMS::Alias
    Properties:
      AliasName: alias/chaos-alert-topic-key
      TargetKeyId: !Ref AlertTopicKey

  AlertTopic:
    Type: AWS::SNS::Topic
    Properties:
      TopicName: chaos-alert-topic
      KmsMasterKeyId: !Ref AlertTopicKey
      DisplayName: Chaos Engineering Alerts

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # IAM roles for Lambda functions and the Step Functions state machine
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  TerminateLambdaRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: lambda.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: TerminateInstancePolicy
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - ec2:TerminateInstances
                Resource:
                  - !Sub arn:${AWS::Partition}:ec2:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:instance/${ChaosInstance}
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - logs:CreateLogGroup
                Resource: '*'
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - logs:CreateLogStream
                  - logs:PutLogEvents
                Resource:
                  - !Sub arn:${AWS::Partition}:logs:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:log-group:/aws/lambda/chaos-terminate-instance:*

  HealthCheckLambdaRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: lambda.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: ServiceHealthCheckPolicy
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - ecs:DescribeServices
                Resource:
                  - !GetAtt ChaosCluster.Arn
                  - !GetAtt ChaosEcsService.ServiceArn
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - sns:Publish
                Resource:
                  - !Ref AlertTopic
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - kms:Decrypt
                  - kms:GenerateDataKey
                Resource:
                  - !GetAtt AlertTopicKey.Arn
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - logs:CreateLogGroup
                Resource: '*'
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - logs:CreateLogStream
                  - logs:PutLogEvents
                Resource:
                  - !Sub arn:${AWS::Partition}:logs:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:log-group:/aws/lambda/chaos-check-service-health:*

  AmiLookupRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: lambda.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: AmiLookupPolicy
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - ec2:DescribeImages
                Resource: '*'
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - logs:CreateLogGroup
                Resource: '*'
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - logs:CreateLogStream
                  - logs:PutLogEvents
                Resource:
                  - !Sub arn:${AWS::Partition}:logs:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:log-group:/aws/lambda/chaos-ami-lookup:*

  StateMachineRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: states.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: StateMachineInvokeLambdasPolicy
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - lambda:InvokeFunction
                Resource:
                  - !GetAtt TerminateChaosInstanceFunction.Arn
                  - !GetAtt CheckServiceHealthFunction.Arn

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Lambda functions
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  TerminateChaosInstanceFunction:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    Properties:
      FunctionName: chaos-terminate-instance
      Handler: index.handler
      Runtime: python3.12
      Role: !GetAtt TerminateLambdaRole.Arn
      Timeout: 60
      MemorySize: 128
      Code:
        ZipFile: |
          import json
          import logging

          import boto3

          logger = logging.getLogger()
          logger.setLevel(logging.INFO)
          ec2 = boto3.client('ec2')


          def handler(event, context):
              logger.info('Event: %s', json.dumps(event))
              instance_id = event.get('instance_id')
              if not instance_id:
                  raise ValueError('Missing required field: instance_id')
              response = ec2.terminate_instances(InstanceIds=[instance_id])
              terminating = response['TerminatingInstances'][0]
              return {
                  'instance_id': instance_id,
                  'previous_state': terminating['PreviousState']['Name'],
                  'current_state': terminating['CurrentState']['Name'],
                  'status_code': 200,
              }

  CheckServiceHealthFunction:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    Properties:
      FunctionName: chaos-check-service-health
      Handler: index.handler
      Runtime: python3.12
      Role: !GetAtt HealthCheckLambdaRole.Arn
      Timeout: 120
      MemorySize: 128
      Code:
        ZipFile: |
          import json
          import logging

          import boto3

          logger = logging.getLogger()
          logger.setLevel(logging.INFO)
          ecs = boto3.client('ecs')
          sns = boto3.client('sns')


          def handler(event, context):
              logger.info('Event: %s', json.dumps(event))
              cluster = event.get('cluster')
              service = event.get('service')
              topic_arn = event.get('topic_arn')

              running = 0
              desired = 0
              try:
                  response = ecs.describe_services(cluster=cluster, services=[service])
                  if not response.get('services'):
                      raise RuntimeError('Service not found in cluster')
                  svc = response['services'][0]
                  running = int(svc.get('runningCount', 0))
                  desired = int(svc.get('desiredCount', 0))
                  is_healthy = desired > 0 and running == desired and svc.get('status') == 'ACTIVE'
              except Exception as exc:
                  logger.warning('Health check failed: %s', exc)
                  is_healthy = False

              alert_sent = False
              if not is_healthy:
                  message = (
                      'Chaos engineering health check FAILED.\n'
                      'Cluster: %s\n'
                      'Service: %s\n'
                      'Running tasks: %s\n'
                      'Desired tasks: %s\n'
                      'The ECS service is unhealthy after terminating the target EC2 instance.'
                  ) % (cluster, service, running, desired)
                  sns.publish(
                      TopicArn=topic_arn,
                      Subject='[Chaos Test] ECS Service Unhealthy',
                      Message=message,
                  )
                  alert_sent = True

              return {
                  'is_healthy': is_healthy,
                  'running_count': running,
                  'desired_count': desired,
                  'alert_sent': alert_sent,
              }

  AmiLookupFunction:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    Properties:
      FunctionName: chaos-ami-lookup
      Handler: index.handler
      Runtime: python3.12
      Role: !GetAtt AmiLookupRole.Arn
      Timeout: 120
      MemorySize: 128
      Code:
        ZipFile: |
          import json
          import logging
          import urllib.request
          import uuid

          import boto3

          logger = logging.getLogger()
          logger.setLevel(logging.INFO)


          def send_response(event, context, status, reason, data, physical_resource_id):
              response_body = {
                  'Status': status,
                  'Reason': reason,
                  'PhysicalResourceId': physical_resource_id,
                  'StackId': event['StackId'],
                  'RequestId': event['RequestId'],
                  'LogicalResourceId': event['LogicalResourceId'],
                  'Data': data,
              }
              bytes_body = json.dumps(response_body).encode('utf-8')
              request = urllib.request.Request(
                  event['ResponseURL'],
                  data=bytes_body,
                  method='PUT',
                  headers={'Content-Type': ''},
              )
              with urllib.request.urlopen(request) as resp:
                  logger.info('CloudFormation response status: %s', resp.status)


          def handler(event, context):
              logger.info('Received event: %s', json.dumps(event))
              physical_id = event.get('PhysicalResourceId') or 'AmiLookup-' + str(uuid.uuid4())
              data = {}
              try:
                  if event['RequestType'] in ('Create', 'Update'):
                      ec2 = boto3.client('ec2')
                      images = ec2.describe_images(
                          Owners=['amazon'],
                          Filters=[
                              {'Name': 'name', 'Values': ['amzn2-ami-hvm-*-x86_64-gp2']},
                              {'Name': 'state', 'Values': ['available']},
                          ],
                      )['Images']
                      if not images:
                          raise RuntimeError('No matching Amazon Linux 2 HVM x86_64 AMI found')
                      images.sort(key=lambda image: image['CreationDate'], reverse=True)
                      data['ImageId'] = images[0]['ImageId']
                      logger.info('Selected AMI: %s', data['ImageId'])
                  send_response(event, context, 'SUCCESS', 'OK', data, physical_id)
              except Exception as exc:
                  logger.exception('AMI lookup failed')
                  send_response(event, context, 'FAILED', str(exc), data, physical_id)
              return data

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Custom resource that resolves the most recent Amazon Linux 2 AMI
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  AmiLookup:
    Type: AWS::CloudFormation::CustomResource
    Properties:
      ServiceToken: !GetAtt AmiLookupFunction.Arn

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Step Functions state machine
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  ChaosStateMachine:
    Type: AWS::StepFunctions::StateMachine
    Properties:
      StateMachineName: chaos-engineering-workflow
      StateMachineType: STANDARD
      RoleArn: !GetAtt StateMachineRole.Arn
      Definition:
        Comment: >-
          Chaos engineering workflow: terminate the target EC2 instance, wait
          300 seconds, check the ECS service health, and publish an SNS alert if
          the service is unhealthy.
        StartAt: TerminateInstance
        States:
          TerminateInstance:
            Type: Task
            Resource: arn:aws:states:::lambda:invoke
            Parameters:
              FunctionName: !GetAtt TerminateChaosInstanceFunction.Arn
              Payload:
                instance_id: !Ref ChaosInstance
            ResultPath: $.terminate_result
            Next: WaitForRecoveryWindow
          WaitForRecoveryWindow:
            Type: Wait
            Seconds: 300
            Next: CheckServiceHealth
          CheckServiceHealth:
            Type: Task
            Resource: arn:aws:states:::lambda:invoke
            Parameters:
              FunctionName: !GetAtt CheckServiceHealthFunction.Arn
              Payload:
                cluster: !GetAtt ChaosCluster.Arn
                service: !GetAtt ChaosEcsService.Name
                topic_arn: !Ref AlertTopic
            ResultPath: $.health_evaluation
            Next: RouteOnHealth
          RouteOnHealth:
            Type: Choice
            Choices:
              - Variable: $.health_evaluation.Payload.is_healthy
                BooleanEquals: true
                Next: ServiceHealthy
            Default: ServiceUnhealthy
          ServiceHealthy:
            Type: Succeed
          ServiceUnhealthy:
            Type: Succeed

Outputs:
  ChaosInstanceId:
    Description: ID of the chaos engineering target EC2 instance
    Value: !Ref ChaosInstance
  EcsClusterArn:
    Description: ARN of the ECS cluster
    Value: !GetAtt ChaosCluster.Arn
  EcsServiceName:
    Description: Name of the ECS service
    Value: !GetAtt ChaosEcsService.Name
  AlertTopicArn:
    Description: ARN of the SNS alert topic
    Value: !Ref AlertTopic
  StateMachineArn:
    Description: ARN of the chaos engineering Step Functions state machine
    Value: !Ref ChaosStateMachine

Parameters:

  AgentSpaceDescription:

    Type: String

    Description: Name for the IAM role that Operator App end-users assume.

  # ==========================================================================

        - PolicyName: AllowCreateServiceLinkedRoles

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: "2010-09-09"
Description: >-
  Creates SSM Parameters under the stack path and a Secrets Manager secret with
  a dynamically generated password, plus a Python 3.12 Lambda function named
  ParameterStoreDemo that retrieves and prints all of them to demonstrate the
  SSM and Secrets Manager APIs.

Resources:
  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Systems Manager Parameter Store
  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  AppEnvironmentParameter:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Parameter
    Properties:
      Type: String
      Name: !Sub "/${AWS::StackName}/app/environment"
      Value: production
      Description: !Sub "Application environment for stack ${AWS::StackName}"

  LogLevelParameter:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Parameter
    Properties:
      Type: String
      Name: !Sub "/${AWS::StackName}/app/log-level"
      Value: INFO
      Description: !Sub "Logging level for stack ${AWS::StackName}"

  DatabasePortParameter:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Parameter
    Properties:
      Type: String
      Name: !Sub "/${AWS::StackName}/config/database/port"
      Value: "5432"
      Description: !Sub "Database port used by stack ${AWS::StackName}"

  FeatureFlagParameter:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Parameter
    Properties:
      Type: String
      Name: !Sub "/${AWS::StackName}/config/feature-flag/security-demo"
      Value: "true"
      Description: !Sub "Feature flag for stack ${AWS::StackName}"

  ApiTokenParameter:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Parameter
    Properties:
      Type: String
      Name: !Sub "/${AWS::StackName}/secret/api-token"
      Value: changeme-demo-token
      Description: !Sub "API token parameter for stack ${AWS::StackName}"

  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Secrets Manager
  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  DemoDatabaseSecret:
    Type: AWS::SecretsManager::Secret
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub "${AWS::StackName}/demo/db-password"
      Description: !Sub "Dynamically generated DB password for stack ${AWS::StackName}"
      GenerateSecretString:
        SecretStringTemplate: '{"username": "demo-user"}'
        GenerateStringKey: password
        PasswordLength: 32
        ExcludePunctuation: true
      Tags:
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: iac-god-eval

  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # IAM role for the Lambda function
  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  ParameterStoreDemoRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: ParameterStoreDemoRole
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: "2012-10-17"
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: lambda.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: ParameterStoreAndSecretsRead
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: "2012-10-17"
            Statement:
              - Sid: ReadSSMParameters
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - ssm:GetParametersByPath
                  - ssm:GetParameters
                  - ssm:GetParameter
                Resource:
                  - !Sub "arn:aws:ssm:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:parameter/${AWS::StackName}/*"
                  - !Sub "arn:aws:ssm:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:parameter/${AWS::StackName}"
              - Sid: ListSecrets
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - secretsmanager:ListSecrets
                Resource: "*"
              - Sid: ReadSecrets
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - secretsmanager:GetSecretValue
                Resource:
                  - !Sub "arn:aws:secretsmanager:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:secret:${AWS::StackName}/*"
      Tags:
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: iac-god-eval

  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Lambda function named ParameterStoreDemo (Python 3.12)
  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  ParameterStoreDemoFunction:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    Properties:
      FunctionName: ParameterStoreDemo
      Description: >-
        Retrieves and prints all SSM parameters under the stack path and all
        Secrets Manager secrets matching the stack prefix.
      Runtime: python3.12
      Handler: index.lambda_handler
      Role: !GetAtt ParameterStoreDemoRole.Arn
      Timeout: 30
      MemorySize: 128
      Environment:
        Variables:
          STACK_NAME: !Ref "AWS::StackName"
      Code:
        ZipFile: |
          import json
          import os

          import boto3

          ssm = boto3.client("ssm")
          secrets_manager = boto3.client("secretsmanager")


          def lambda_handler(event, context):
              stack_name = os.environ["STACK_NAME"]
              path = "/{}/".format(stack_name)

              parameters = {}
              ssm_paginator = ssm.get_paginator("get_parameters_by_path")
              for page in ssm_paginator.paginate(
                  Path=path, Recursive=True, WithDecryption=True
              ):
                  for parameter in page.get("Parameters", []):
                      parameters[parameter["Name"]] = parameter["Value"]

              secrets = {}
              sm_paginator = secrets_manager.get_paginator("list_secrets")
              for page in sm_paginator.paginate(
                  Filters=[{"Key": "name", "Values": [stack_name + "/"]}]
              ):
                  for secret in page.get("SecretList", []):
                      name = secret["Name"]
                      try:
                          value = secrets_manager.get_secret_value(SecretId=name)
                          secret_string = value.get("SecretString")
                          if not secret_string:
                              binary = value.get("SecretBinary")
                              if binary is not None:
                                  secret_string = binary.decode("utf-8")
                          secrets[name] = secret_string
                      except Exception as exc:
                          secrets[name] = "<error retrieving: {}>".format(exc)

              print("SSM parameters under path '{}':".format(path))
              for name, value in sorted(parameters.items()):
                  print("  {} = {}".format(name, value))

              print("Secrets matching prefix '{}':".format(stack_name))
              for name, value in sorted(secrets.items()):
                  print("  {} = {}".format(name, value))

              return {
                  "statusCode": 200,
                  "body": json.dumps(
                      {"parameters": parameters, "secrets": secrets},
                      indent=2,
                      default=str,
                  ),
              }
      Tags:
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: iac-god-eval

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: "2010-09-09"
Description: >-
  Provisions a custom Systems Manager (SSM) Inventory collection mechanism that
  tracks running database and caching processes on Windows and Linux EC2
  instances. The stack deploys an SSM Command document containing shell and
  PowerShell steps that resolve the instance ID from instance metadata, search
  for configured process keywords, and write the results into the SSM custom
  inventory directory, together with an SSM association named
  'Custom-Inventory-Processes' that runs the document against all instances on
  the specified schedule.

Parameters:
  LinuxProcessKeywords:
    Type: String
    Description: >-
      Comma-separated process keywords used to detect database and caching
      processes on Linux instances.
    Default: "CassandraDaemon,dse cassandra,mysql,postgres,redis-server,redis-sentinel,memcached"
  WindowsProcessKeywords:
    Type: String
    Description: >-
      Comma-separated process keywords used to detect database and caching
      processes on Windows instances.
    Default: "sqlservr,cassandra,mysql,postgres,redis-server,redis-sentinel,memcached"
  ScheduleExpression:
    Type: String
    Description: >-
      Rate or cron expression that defines how often the custom inventory
      collection association runs.
    Default: "rate(30 days)"

Resources:
  CustomInventoryDocument:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Document
    Properties:
      Name: Custom-Inventory-Processes
      DocumentType: Command
      Content:
        schemaVersion: "2.2"
        description: >-
          Collects custom SSM inventory for database and caching processes on
          Windows and Linux managed nodes.
        parameters:
          LinuxProcessKeywords:
            type: String
            description: Comma-separated process keywords for Linux instances.
            default: "CassandraDaemon,dse cassandra,mysql,postgres,redis-server,redis-sentinel,memcached"
          WindowsProcessKeywords:
            type: String
            description: Comma-separated process keywords for Windows instances.
            default: "sqlservr,cassandra,mysql,postgres,redis-server,redis-sentinel,memcached"
        mainSteps:
          - name: collectLinuxProcessInventory
            action: aws:runShellScript
            precondition:
              StringEquals:
                - platformType
                - Linux
            inputs:
              timeoutSeconds: "300"
              runCommand:
                - |
                  #!/bin/bash
                  set -euo pipefail

                  echo "Collecting custom process inventory (Linux)"

                  IMDS_TOKEN=""
                  if curl -s -m 2 -X PUT "http://169.254.169.254/latest/api/token" -H "X-aws-ec2-metadata-token-ttl-seconds: 21600" -o /tmp/custom_inv_token 2>/dev/null; then
                    IMDS_TOKEN=$(cat /tmp/custom_inv_token 2>/dev/null || true)
                  fi
                  if [ -n "${IMDS_TOKEN}" ]; then
                    INSTANCE_ID=$(curl -s -m 2 -H "X-aws-ec2-metadata-token: ${IMDS_TOKEN}" http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/instance-id 2>/dev/null || true)
                  else
                    INSTANCE_ID=$(curl -s -m 2 http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/instance-id 2>/dev/null || true)
                  fi
                  rm -f /tmp/custom_inv_token

                  if [ -z "${INSTANCE_ID:-}" ]; then
                    echo "ERROR: unable to determine the instance ID from instance metadata" >&2
                    exit 1
                  fi
                  echo "Instance ID resolved: ${INSTANCE_ID}"

                  INV_CUSTOM_DIR="/var/lib/amazon/ssm/${INSTANCE_ID}/inventory/custom"
                  mkdir -p "${INV_CUSTOM_DIR}"

                  export KEYWORDS_RAW="{{ LinuxProcessKeywords }}"

                  if command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                    ps -eo pid=,user=,comm=,args= --no-headers 2>/dev/null > /tmp/custom_inv_processes.txt || true
                    python3 - "${INSTANCE_ID}" "${INV_CUSTOM_DIR}" <<'PYEOF'
                  import json
                  import os
                  import re
                  import sys
                  from datetime import datetime, timezone

                  instance_id = sys.argv[1]
                  inv_dir = sys.argv[2]
                  keywords = [k.strip() for k in os.environ.get('KEYWORDS_RAW', '').split(',') if k.strip()]

                  try:
                      with open('/tmp/custom_inv_processes.txt', 'r', errors='replace') as handle:
                          lines = handle.read().splitlines()
                  except FileNotFoundError:
                      lines = []

                  results = []
                  for keyword in keywords:
                      pattern = re.compile(re.escape(keyword), re.IGNORECASE)
                      matched = []
                      for line in lines:
                          if pattern.search(line):
                              parts = line.split(None, 3)
                              entry = {'pid': parts[0] if parts else ''}
                              if len(parts) > 1:
                                  entry['user'] = parts[1]
                              if len(parts) > 2:
                                  entry['name'] = parts[2]
                              if len(parts) > 3:
                                  entry['command_line'] = parts[3]
                              matched.append(entry)
                      results.append({'keyword': keyword, 'count': len(matched), 'processes': matched})

                  payload = {
                      'SchemaVersion': '1.0',
                      'TypeName': 'Custom:DatabaseCacheProcessInventory',
                      'Content': {
                          'InstanceId': instance_id,
                          'CollectedAt': datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ'),
                          'Processes': results,
                      },
                  }

                  inventory_file = os.path.join(inv_dir, 'CustomInventory.json')
                  with open(inventory_file, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as out:
                      json.dump(payload, out, indent=2)
                  print('Custom inventory written to {}'.format(inventory_file))
                  PYEOF
                  else
                    echo "WARN: python3 not found, writing compact custom inventory"
                    {
                      echo '{'
                      echo '  "SchemaVersion": "1.0",'
                      echo '  "TypeName": "Custom:DatabaseCacheProcessInventory",'
                      echo '  "Content": {'
                      echo '    "InstanceId": "'"${INSTANCE_ID}"'",'
                      echo '    "Processes": {'
                      FIRST=1
                      OLD_IFS="${IFS}"
                      IFS=','
                      for KW in ${KEYWORDS_RAW}; do
                        KW=$(echo "${KW}" | sed -e 's/^[[:space:]]*//' -e 's/[[:space:]]*$//')
                        if [ -z "${KW}" ]; then
                          continue
                        fi
                        COUNT=$(pgrep -f "${KW}" 2>/dev/null | wc -l || true)
                        if [ "${FIRST}" -eq 1 ]; then
                          FIRST=0
                        else
                          echo ','
                        fi
                        echo -n '      "'"${KW}"'": '"${COUNT}"
                      done
                      echo ''
                      IFS="${OLD_IFS}"
                      echo '    }'
                      echo '  }'
                      echo '}'
                    } > "${INV_CUSTOM_DIR}/CustomInventory.json"
                  fi

                  echo "Custom inventory collection completed"
          - name: collectWindowsProcessInventory
            action: aws:runPowerShellScript
            precondition:
              StringEquals:
                - platformType
                - Windows
            inputs:
              timeoutSeconds: "300"
              runCommand:
                - |
                  $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
                  Write-Output "Collecting custom process inventory (Windows)"

                  $InstanceId = $null
                  try {
                      $Token = Invoke-RestMethod -Method Put -Uri "http://169.254.169.254/latest/api/token" -Headers @{ "X-aws-ec2-metadata-token-ttl-seconds" = "21600" } -TimeoutSec 5
                      $InstanceId = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri "http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/instance-id" -Headers @{ "X-aws-ec2-metadata-token" = $Token } -TimeoutSec 5
                  } catch {
                      try {
                          $InstanceId = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri "http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/instance-id" -TimeoutSec 5
                      } catch {
                          throw "Unable to determine the instance ID from instance metadata: $($_.Exception.Message)"
                      }
                  }

                  if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($InstanceId)) {
                      throw "Instance ID could not be resolved from instance metadata"
                  }
                  Write-Output "Instance ID resolved: $InstanceId"

                  $Keywords = @("{{ WindowsProcessKeywords }}".Split(",") | ForEach-Object { $_.Trim() } | Where-Object { $_ -ne "" })
                  if ($Keywords.Count -eq 0) {
                      throw "No process keywords were provided for Windows inventory collection"
                  }

                  $Results = @()
                  foreach ($Keyword in $Keywords) {
                      $Pattern = [regex]::Escape($Keyword)
                      $MatchedProcesses = @()
                      try {
                          $MatchedProcesses = @(Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object {
                              ($null -ne $_.Name -and $_.Name -match $Pattern) -or ($null -ne $_.CommandLine -and $_.CommandLine -match $Pattern)
                          })
                      } catch {
                          Write-Output "WARN: unable to enumerate processes for keyword '$Keyword': $($_.Exception.Message)"
                      }

                      $ProcessDetails = @()
                      foreach ($Process in $MatchedProcesses) {
                          $ProcessDetails += @{
                              pid = $Process.ProcessId
                              name = $Process.Name
                              executable = $Process.ExecutablePath
                              command_line = $Process.CommandLine
                          }
                      }

                      $Results += @{
                          keyword = $Keyword
                          count = $ProcessDetails.Count
                          processes = @($ProcessDetails)
                      }
                  }

                  $InventoryDir = "C:\ProgramData\Amazon\SSM\InstanceData\$InstanceId\inventory\custom"
                  New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $InventoryDir -Force | Out-Null

                      Content = @{

                          CollectedAt = [DateTime]::UtcNow.ToString("yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ")
                          Processes = @($Results)
                      }
                  }

                  $Json = $Payload | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 10
                  $InventoryFile = Join-Path $InventoryDir "CustomInventory.json"
                  [System.IO.File]::WriteAllText($InventoryFile, $Json, (New-Object System.Text.UTF8Encoding($false)))
