AWSTemplateFormatVersion: "2010-09-09"

Description: >
  Creates an Amazon DataZone domain with a configurable domain name (default:
  cookbookChapter11), producer and consumer projects (SalesPublisher and
  MarketingConsumer), the IAM roles required for domain execution, data access
  (Glue, Redshift, and Secrets Manager) and environment provisioning, and enables
  the DefaultDataWarehouse environment blueprint in the current region.

Parameters:
  DomainName:
    Type: String
    Default: cookbookChapter11
    MinLength: 1
    MaxLength: 64
    AllowedPattern: "^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$"
    Description: Name of the Amazon DataZone domain to create.
    ConstraintDescription: >
      The domain name must be 1-64 characters and may contain only letters,
      numbers, hyphens, and underscores.

  DomainDescription:
    Type: String
    Default: Amazon DataZone domain for the DataZone cookbook, chapter 11.
    Description: Description of the Amazon DataZone domain.

Resources:
  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # IAM role assumed by Amazon DataZone for domain execution.
  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  DataZoneDomainExecutionRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: DataZoneDomainExecutionRole
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: "2012-10-17"
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: datazone.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - !Sub arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AmazonDataZoneDomainExecutionRolePolicy
      Tags:
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: iac-god-eval

  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # IAM role used for data access by DataZone projects and data sources,
  # including Glue, Redshift, and Secrets Manager permissions.
  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  DataZoneDataAccessRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: DataZoneDataAccessRole
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: "2012-10-17"
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service:
                - datazone.amazonaws.com
                - glue.amazonaws.com
                - redshift.amazonaws.com
                - lakeformation.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: DataZoneDataAccessPolicy
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: "2012-10-17"
            Statement:
              - Sid: GlueDataAccess
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - glue:GetDatabase
                  - glue:GetDatabases
                  - glue:GetTable
                  - glue:GetTables
                  - glue:GetPartition
                  - glue:GetPartitions
                  - glue:BatchGetPartition
                  - glue:GetColumnStatisticsForPartition
                  - glue:GetColumnStatisticsForTable
                  - glue:GetUserDefinedFunction
                  - glue:GetUserDefinedFunctions
                  - glue:SearchTables
                  - glue:CreateDatabase
                  - glue:UpdateDatabase
                  - glue:CreateTable
                  - glue:UpdateTable
                  - glue:CreatePartition
                  - glue:UpdatePartition
                  - glue:DeletePartition
                Resource: "*"
              - Sid: RedshiftDataAccess
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - redshift:DescribeClusters
                  - redshift:DescribeClusterSnapshots
                  - redshift:DescribeClusterSubnetGroups
                  - redshift:DescribeEvents
                  - redshift:DescribeLoggingStatus
                  - redshift-data:ExecuteStatement
                  - redshift-data:DescribeStatement
                  - redshift-data:GetStatementResult
                  - redshift-data:CancelStatement
                  - redshift-data:ListStatements
                  - redshift-data:ListDatabases
                  - redshift-data:ListSchemas
                  - redshift-data:ListTables
                  - redshift-serverless:GetNamespace
                  - redshift-serverless:GetWorkgroup
                  - redshift-serverless:ListNamespaces
                  - redshift-serverless:ListWorkgroups
                  - redshift-serverless:ListTagsForResource
                Resource: "*"
              - Sid: SecretsManagerDataAccess
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - secretsmanager:GetSecretValue
                  - secretsmanager:DescribeSecret
                  - secretsmanager:ListSecrets
                  - secretsmanager:GetResourcePolicy
                Resource: "*"
              - Sid: DataLakeDataAccess
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - s3:ListAllMyBuckets
                  - s3:ListBucket
                  - s3:GetBucketLocation
                  - s3:GetObject
                  - s3:GetObjectVersion
                  - s3:GetObjectAcl
                  - s3:GetObjectTagging
                  - lakeformation:GetDataAccess
                  - lakeformation:ListPermissions
                  - athena:StartQueryExecution
                  - athena:GetQueryExecution
                  - athena:GetQueryResults
                  - athena:GetDataCatalog
                  - athena:ListDataCatalogs
                  - athena:GetWorkGroup
                  - athena:ListWorkGroups
                Resource: "*"
      Tags:
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: iac-god-eval

  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # IAM role used to provision environments (DefaultDataWarehouse blueprint)
  # for the DataZone domain.
  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  DataZoneProvisioningRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: DataZoneProvisioningRole
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: "2012-10-17"
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service:
                - datazone.amazonaws.com
                - cloudformation.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - !Sub arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::aws:policy/AmazonDataZoneRedshiftGlueProvisioningPolicy
      Tags:
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: iac-god-eval

  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Amazon DataZone domain.
  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  DataZoneDomain:
    Type: AWS::DataZone::Domain
    Properties:
      Name: !Ref DomainName
      Description: !Ref DomainDescription
      DomainExecutionRole: !GetAtt DataZoneDomainExecutionRole.Arn
      Tags:
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: iac-god-eval

  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Producer project (sales data publishing team).
  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  SalesPublisherProject:
    Type: AWS::DataZone::Project
    Properties:
      DomainIdentifier: !Ref DataZoneDomain
      Name: SalesPublisher
      Description: Producer team project for publishing sales data assets.

  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Consumer project (marketing analytics team).
  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  MarketingConsumerProject:
    Type: AWS::DataZone::Project
    Properties:
      DomainIdentifier: !Ref DataZoneDomain
      Name: MarketingConsumer
      Description: Consumer team project for analyzing sales and marketing data.

  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Enable the DefaultDataWarehouse environment blueprint in the current region.
  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  DefaultDataWarehouseBlueprintConfiguration:
    Type: AWS::DataZone::EnvironmentBlueprintConfiguration
    Properties:
      DomainIdentifier: !Ref DataZoneDomain
      EnvironmentBlueprintIdentifier: DefaultDataWarehouse
      EnabledRegions:
        - !Ref AWS::Region
      ProvisioningRoleArn: !GetAtt DataZoneProvisioningRole.Arn

Outputs:
  DataZoneDomainId:
    Description: Identifier of the Amazon DataZone domain.
    Value: !Ref DataZoneDomain
  DataZoneDomainArn:
    Description: ARN of the Amazon DataZone domain.
    Value: !GetAtt DataZoneDomain.Arn
  DataZoneDataPortalUrl:
    Description: URL of the Amazon DataZone data portal.
    Value: !GetAtt DataZoneDomain.PortalUrl
  DomainExecutionRoleArn:
    Description: ARN of the domain execution role.
    Value: !GetAtt DataZoneDomainExecutionRole.Arn
  DataAccessRoleArn:
    Description: ARN of the data access role.
    Value: !GetAtt DataZoneDataAccessRole.Arn
  ProvisioningRoleArn:
    Description: ARN of the environment provisioning role.
    Value: !GetAtt DataZoneProvisioningRole.Arn
  SalesPublisherProjectId:
    Description: Identifier of the SalesPublisher project.
    Value: !Ref SalesPublisherProject
  MarketingConsumerProjectId:
    Description: Identifier of the MarketingConsumer project.
    Value: !Ref MarketingConsumerProject
  DefaultDataWarehouseBlueprintConfigurationId:
    Description: Identifier of the DefaultDataWarehouse blueprint configuration.
    Value: !Ref DefaultDataWarehouseBlueprintConfiguration

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: 'App Mesh colorteller demo service'

Resources:
  # Cloud Map namespace and service for service discovery
  CloudMapNamespace:
    Type: AWS::ServiceDiscovery::HttpNamespace
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub "${AWS::StackName}.local"

  CloudMapService:
    Type: AWS::ServiceDiscovery::Service
    Properties:
      Name: colorteller
      NamespaceId: !Ref CloudMapNamespace

  # App Mesh
  Mesh:
    Type: AWS::AppMesh::Mesh
    Properties:
      MeshName: !Ref AWS::StackName

  # Virtual Nodes
  BlueNode:
    Type: AWS::AppMesh::VirtualNode
    DependsOn: Mesh
    Properties:
      MeshName: !Ref AWS::StackName
      VirtualNodeName: colorteller-blue-node
      Spec:
        Listeners:
          - PortMapping:
              Port: 9080
              Protocol: http
            HealthCheck:
              HealthyThreshold: 2
              UnhealthyThreshold: 2
              TimeoutMillis: 2000
              IntervalMillis: 5000
              Path: /ping
              Protocol: http
        ServiceDiscovery:
          AWSCloudMap:
            NamespaceName: !Sub "${AWS::StackName}.local"
            ServiceName: colorteller

  GreenNode:
    Type: AWS::AppMesh::VirtualNode
    DependsOn: Mesh
    Properties:
      MeshName: !Ref AWS::StackName
      VirtualNodeName: colorteller-green-node
      Spec:
        Listeners:
          - PortMapping:
              Port: 9080
              Protocol: http
            HealthCheck:
              HealthyThreshold: 2
              UnhealthyThreshold: 2
              TimeoutMillis: 2000
              IntervalMillis: 5000
              Path: /ping
              Protocol: http
        ServiceDiscovery:
          AWSCloudMap:
            NamespaceName: !Sub "${AWS::StackName}.local"
            ServiceName: colorteller

  # Virtual Router
  Router:
    Type: AWS::AppMesh::VirtualRouter
    DependsOn: Mesh
    Properties:
      MeshName: !Ref AWS::StackName
      VirtualRouterName: colorteller-router
      Spec:
        Listeners:
          - PortMapping:
              Port: 9080
              Protocol: http

  # Route - splits traffic 50/50 between blue and green
  Route:
    Type: AWS::AppMesh::Route
    Properties:
      MeshName: !Ref AWS::StackName
      VirtualRouterName: !GetAtt Router.VirtualRouterName
      RouteName: colorteller-route
      Spec:
        HttpRoute:
          Action:

              - VirtualNode: !GetAtt BlueNode.VirtualNodeName

              - VirtualNode: !GetAtt GreenNode.VirtualNodeName

  # Virtual Service - routes through the virtual router
  VirtualService:
    Type: AWS::AppMesh::VirtualService
    Properties:
      MeshName: !Ref AWS::StackName
      VirtualServiceName: colorteller
      Spec:
        Provider:
          VirtualRouter:
            VirtualRouterName: !GetAtt Router.VirtualRouterName

  VirtualGateway:
    Type: AWS::AppMesh::VirtualGateway
    DependsOn: Mesh
    Properties:

      VirtualGatewayName: colorgateway
      Spec:
        Listeners:

              Port: 9080
              Protocol: http
            HealthCheck:
              HealthyThreshold: 2
              UnhealthyThreshold: 2
              TimeoutMillis: 2000
              IntervalMillis: 5000
              Path: /ping
              Protocol: http

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: "2010-09-09"
Description: >-
  Creates private S3 buckets for a data processing pipeline: a source bucket, a
  target bucket, and an optional EMR log bucket that is only created when the
  EnableEmrLogBucket parameter is true. All buckets have lifecycle rules that
  transition objects to STANDARD_IA or GLACIER after 90 days (depending on the
  region) and expire objects after 2555 days; the lifecycle rule is enabled only
  on the EMR log bucket. Bucket names and the DNS name of the EMR log bucket are
  exported for cross-stack reference.

Parameters:
  EnableEmrLogBucket:
    Type: String
    AllowedValues:
      - "true"
      - "false"
    Default: "false"
    Description: >-
      Whether to create the optional EMR log bucket. Set to true to create it.

Conditions:
  # Create the EMR log bucket only when EnableEmrLogBucket is "true".
  CreateEmrLogBucket: !Equals [!Ref EnableEmrLogBucket, "true"]
  # Use STANDARD_IA as the post-90-day storage class in common regions and
  # GLACIER everywhere else.
  UseStandardIAStorage: !Or
    - !Equals [!Ref "AWS::Region", "us-east-1"]
    - !Equals [!Ref "AWS::Region", "us-east-2"]
    - !Equals [!Ref "AWS::Region", "us-west-1"]
    - !Equals [!Ref "AWS::Region", "us-west-2"]
    - !Equals [!Ref "AWS::Region", "eu-west-1"]
    - !Equals [!Ref "AWS::Region", "eu-central-1"]
    - !Equals [!Ref "AWS::Region", "ap-south-1"]
    - !Equals [!Ref "AWS::Region", "ap-northeast-1"]
    - !Equals [!Ref "AWS::Region", "ap-southeast-1"]
    - !Equals [!Ref "AWS::Region", "ap-southeast-2"]

Resources:
  EncryptionKey:
    Type: AWS::KMS::Key
    Properties:
      Description: >-
        Customer managed KMS key used to encrypt the data processing pipeline
        S3 buckets (source, target and EMR log buckets).
      Enabled: true
      EnableKeyRotation: true
      KeyPolicy:
        Version: "2012-10-17"
        Id: kms-key-default-policy
        Statement:
          - Sid: Enable IAM User Permissions
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              AWS: !Sub "arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::${AWS::AccountId}:root"
            Action: "kms:*"
            Resource: "*"
  SourceBucket:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
    Properties:
      AccessControl: Private
      BucketEncryption:
        ServerSideEncryptionConfiguration:
          - ServerSideEncryptionByDefault:
              SSEAlgorithm: aws:kms
              KMSMasterKeyID: !Ref EncryptionKey
            BucketKeyEnabled: true
      PublicAccessBlockConfiguration:
        BlockPublicAcls: true
        BlockPublicPolicy: true
        IgnorePublicAcls: true
        RestrictPublicBuckets: true
      LifecycleConfiguration:
        Rules:
          - Id: SourceBucketLifecycleRule
            Status: Disabled
            Transitions:
              - StorageClass: !If [UseStandardIAStorage, "STANDARD_IA", "GLACIER"]
                TransitionInDays: 90
            ExpirationInDays: 2555

  TargetBucket:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
    Properties:
      AccessControl: Private
      BucketEncryption:
        ServerSideEncryptionConfiguration:
          - ServerSideEncryptionByDefault:
              SSEAlgorithm: aws:kms
              KMSMasterKeyID: !Ref EncryptionKey
            BucketKeyEnabled: true
      PublicAccessBlockConfiguration:
        BlockPublicAcls: true
        BlockPublicPolicy: true
        IgnorePublicAcls: true
        RestrictPublicBuckets: true
      LifecycleConfiguration:
        Rules:
          - Id: TargetBucketLifecycleRule
            Status: Disabled
            Transitions:
              - StorageClass: !If [UseStandardIAStorage, "STANDARD_IA", "GLACIER"]
                TransitionInDays: 90
            ExpirationInDays: 2555

  EmrLogBucket:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
    Condition: CreateEmrLogBucket
    Properties:
      AccessControl: Private
      BucketEncryption:
        ServerSideEncryptionConfiguration:
          - ServerSideEncryptionByDefault:
              SSEAlgorithm: aws:kms
              KMSMasterKeyID: !Ref EncryptionKey
            BucketKeyEnabled: true
      PublicAccessBlockConfiguration:
        BlockPublicAcls: true
        BlockPublicPolicy: true
        IgnorePublicAcls: true
        RestrictPublicBuckets: true
      LifecycleConfiguration:
        Rules:
          - Id: EmrLogBucketLifecycleRule
            Status: Enabled
            Transitions:
              - StorageClass: !If [UseStandardIAStorage, "STANDARD_IA", "GLACIER"]
                TransitionInDays: 90
            ExpirationInDays: 2555

Outputs:
  SourceBucketName:
    Description: Name of the source S3 bucket
    Value: !Ref SourceBucket
    Export:
      Name: !Sub "${AWS::StackName}-SourceBucketName"

  TargetBucketName:
    Description: Name of the target S3 bucket
    Value: !Ref TargetBucket
    Export:
      Name: !Sub "${AWS::StackName}-TargetBucketName"

  EmrLogBucketName:
    Description: Name of the EMR log S3 bucket
    Condition: CreateEmrLogBucket
    Value: !Ref EmrLogBucket
    Export:
      Name: !Sub "${AWS::StackName}-EmrLogBucketName"

  EmrLogBucketDomainName:
    Description: DNS (domain) name of the EMR log S3 bucket
    Condition: CreateEmrLogBucket
    Value: !GetAtt EmrLogBucket.DomainName
    Export:
      Name: !Sub "${AWS::StackName}-EmrLogBucketDomainName"

  EmrLogBucketRegionalDomainName:
    Description: Regional DNS (domain) name of the EMR log S3 bucket
    Condition: CreateEmrLogBucket
    Value: !GetAtt EmrLogBucket.RegionalDomainName
    Export:
      Name: !Sub "${AWS::StackName}-EmrLogBucketRegionalDomainName"

  AppSync GraphQL API with IAM authentication, a Note type with getNote and
  saveNote operations, and an Amazon EventBridge data source that puts events
  onto a custom EventBridge event bus.

Resources:
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Custom EventBridge Event Bus
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  NoteEventBus:
    Type: AWS::Events::EventBus

        Version: "2012-10-17"
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: appsync.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: EventBridgePutEvents
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: "2012-10-17"
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action: events:PutEvents
                Resource: !GetAtt NoteEventBus.Arn

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # AppSync GraphQL API with IAM authentication
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  NoteApi:
    Type: AWS::AppSync::GraphQLApi

        - !Split

          NoteId: ID!
          title: String!
          content: String

          getNote(NoteId: ID!): Note

          saveNote(NoteId: ID!, title: String!, content: String): Note

              "detailType": "NoteQueried",
              "detail": $util.toJson($ctx.args)

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: >-
  Scheduled Lambda function that removes expired items from the DynamoDB
  table "throttle" by scanning the table and deleting expired records in
  batches. The schedule runs hourly by default and can be disabled by
  supplying an empty string for the ScheduleExpression parameter.

Parameters:
  ScheduleExpression:
    Type: String
    Default: rate(1 hour)
    Description: >-
      EventBridge schedule expression that triggers the cleanup function
      (for example "rate(1 hour)" or "cron(0 * * * ? *)"). Pass an empty
      string to disable the scheduled trigger entirely.

Conditions:
  ScheduleEnabled: !Not
    - !Equals
      - !Ref ScheduleExpression
      - ''

Resources:
  CleanupTable:
    Type: AWS::DynamoDB::Table
    Properties:
      TableName: throttle
      BillingMode: PAY_PER_REQUEST
      AttributeDefinitions:
        - AttributeName: id
          AttributeType: S
        - AttributeName: expiresAt
          AttributeType: N
      KeySchema:
        - AttributeName: id
          KeyType: HASH
        - AttributeName: expiresAt
          KeyType: RANGE
      SSESpecification:
        SSEEnabled: true
      PointInTimeRecoverySpecification:
        PointInTimeRecoveryEnabled: true
      DeletionProtectionEnabled: false

  CleanupLogGroup:
    Type: AWS::Logs::LogGroup
    Properties:
      LogGroupName: /aws/lambda/DynamoDBCleanupFunction
      RetentionInDays: 30

  CleanupFunctionRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: lambda.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: DynamoDBCleanupPolicy
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - dynamodb:Scan
                  - dynamodb:BatchWriteItem
                Resource: !GetAtt CleanupTable.Arn
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - logs:CreateLogStream
                  - logs:PutLogEvents
                Resource: !Sub
                  - '${LogGroupArn}:*'
                  - LogGroupArn: !GetAtt CleanupLogGroup.Arn

  CleanupFunction:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    DependsOn: CleanupLogGroup
    Properties:
      FunctionName: DynamoDBCleanupFunction
      Description: Deletes expired items from the throttle DynamoDB table in batches.
      Runtime: python3.12
      Handler: index.handler
      Timeout: 300
      MemorySize: 256
      Role: !GetAtt CleanupFunctionRole.Arn
      TracingConfig:
        Mode: Active
      Code:
        ZipFile: |
          import os
          import time

          import boto3

          TABLE_NAME = os.environ.get("TABLE_NAME", "throttle")
          DELETE_BATCH_SIZE = 25

          _dynamodb = boto3.resource("dynamodb")
          _table = _dynamodb.Table(TABLE_NAME)


          def handler(event, context):
              """Delete expired items (expiresAt < now) in batches of 25."""
              now = int(time.time())
              deleted = 0
              scan_kwargs = {
                  "FilterExpression": "#expires < :now",
                  "ExpressionAttributeNames": {"#expires": "expiresAt"},
                  "ExpressionAttributeValues": {":now": now},
                  "ProjectionExpression": "id, expiresAt",
              }

              while True:
                  response = _table.scan(**scan_kwargs)
                  items = response.get("Items", [])
                  for start in range(0, len(items), DELETE_BATCH_SIZE):
                      chunk = items[start:start + DELETE_BATCH_SIZE]
                      with _table.batch_writer() as batch:
                          for item in chunk:
                              batch.delete_item(
                                  Key={
                                      "id": item["id"],
                                      "expiresAt": item["expiresAt"],
                                  }
                              )
                      deleted += len(chunk)

                  last_key = response.get("LastEvaluatedKey")
                  if not last_key:
                      break
                  scan_kwargs["ExclusiveStartKey"] = last_key

              print(f"Deleted {deleted} expired items from {TABLE_NAME}")
              return {"deleted": deleted}

  CleanupSchedule:
    Type: AWS::Events::Rule
    Condition: ScheduleEnabled
    Properties:
      Description: Hourly trigger for the DynamoDB expired item cleanup function.
      ScheduleExpression: !Ref ScheduleExpression
      State: ENABLED
      Targets:
        - Id: DynamoDBCleanupTarget
          Arn: !GetAtt CleanupFunction.Arn

  CleanupSchedulePermission:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Permission
    Condition: ScheduleEnabled
    Properties:
      Action: lambda:InvokeFunction
      FunctionName: !Ref CleanupFunction
      Principal: events.amazonaws.com
      SourceArn: !GetAtt CleanupSchedule.Arn

Outputs:
  TableName:
    Description: Name of the DynamoDB table holding the cleanup records.
    Value: !Ref CleanupTable
  FunctionName:
    Description: Name of the scheduled cleanup Lambda function.
    Value: !Ref CleanupFunction
  ScheduleState:
    Description: Whether the scheduled trigger is enabled.
    Value: !If
      - ScheduleEnabled
      - Enabled
      - Disabled

Description: >-
  AWS IoT SiteWise wind farm demo asset models. Creates a wind turbine asset
  model with attributes, measurements, transforms and metrics, plus a wind farm
  asset model that rolls up the turbine metrics over a 5-minute tumbling window.

Resources:
  TurbineAssetModel:
    Type: AWS::IoTSiteWise::AssetModel
    Properties:
      AssetModelName: Wind Turbine Asset Model
      AssetModelDescription: >-
        Asset model for the wind turbines of the wind farm demo. Measurements
        are ingested per turbine, transforms derive power and overdrive state,
        and metrics aggregate the values over a 5-minute tumbling window.
      AssetModelProperties:
        - Name: Turbine Manufacturer
          LogicalId: TurbineManufacturer
          DataType: STRING
          Type:
            TypeName: Attribute
            Attribute:
              DefaultValue: Demo Turbines Inc.
        - Name: Rated Power
          LogicalId: RatedPower
          DataType: DOUBLE
          Unit: kW
          Type:
            TypeName: Attribute
            Attribute:
              DefaultValue: "2500"
        - Name: Wind Speed
          LogicalId: WindSpeed
          DataType: DOUBLE
          Unit: m/s
          Type:
            TypeName: Measurement
        - Name: Rotational Speed
          LogicalId: RotationalSpeed
          DataType: DOUBLE
          Unit: RPM
          Type:
            TypeName: Measurement
        - Name: Torque
          LogicalId: Torque
          DataType: DOUBLE
          Unit: Nm
          Type:
            TypeName: Measurement
        - Name: Temperature
          LogicalId: Temperature
          DataType: DOUBLE
          Unit: C
          Type:
            TypeName: Measurement
        - Name: Power
          LogicalId: Power
          DataType: DOUBLE
          Unit: kW
          Type:
            TypeName: Transform
            Transform:
              Expression: torque * rotational_speed * 0.10472
              Variables:
                - Name: torque
                  Value:
                    PropertyLogicalId: Torque
                - Name: rotational_speed
                  Value:
                    PropertyLogicalId: RotationalSpeed
        - Name: Overdrive State
          LogicalId: OverdriveState
          DataType: DOUBLE
          Type:
            TypeName: Transform
            Transform:
              Expression: if(gt(torque, 3), 1.0, 0.0)
              Variables:
                - Name: torque
                  Value:
                    PropertyLogicalId: Torque
        - Name: Average Wind Speed
          LogicalId: AverageWindSpeed
          DataType: DOUBLE
          Unit: m/s
          Type:
            TypeName: Metric
            Metric:
              Expression: avg(wind_speed)
              Variables:
                - Name: wind_speed
                  Value:
                    PropertyLogicalId: WindSpeed
              Window:
                Tumbling:
                  Interval: 5m
        - Name: Overdrive State Time
          LogicalId: OverdriveStateTime
          DataType: DOUBLE
          Unit: s
          Type:
            TypeName: Metric
            Metric:
              Expression: statetime(overdrive_state)
              Variables:
                - Name: overdrive_state
                  Value:
                    PropertyLogicalId: OverdriveState
              Window:
                Tumbling:
                  Interval: 5m
        - Name: Average Power
          LogicalId: AveragePower
          DataType: DOUBLE
          Unit: kW
          Type:
            TypeName: Metric
            Metric:
              Expression: avg(power)
              Variables:
                - Name: power
                  Value:
                    PropertyLogicalId: Power
              Window:
                Tumbling:
                  Interval: 5m

    Type: AWS::IoTSiteWise::AssetModel
    Properties:

      AssetModelDescription: >-
        Asset model for the wind farm demo. Aggregates the turbine metrics of

        - Name: Wind Farm Location
          LogicalId: WindFarmLocation
          DataType: STRING
          Type:
            TypeName: Attribute
            Attribute:
              DefaultValue: Oregon, USA
        - Name: Number of Turbines
          LogicalId: NumberOfTurbines
          DataType: INTEGER
          Type:
            TypeName: Attribute
            Attribute:
              DefaultValue: "10"
        - Name: Average Wind Speed
          LogicalId: AverageWindSpeed
          DataType: DOUBLE
          Unit: m/s
          Type:
            TypeName: Metric
            Metric:
              Expression: avg(average_wind_speed)
              Variables:
                - Name: average_wind_speed
                  Value:
                    PropertyLogicalId: AverageWindSpeed
                    HierarchyLogicalId: TurbineHierarchy
              Window:
                Tumbling:
                  Interval: 5m
        - Name: Total Overdrive State Time
          LogicalId: TotalOverdriveStateTime
          DataType: DOUBLE
          Unit: s
          Type:
            TypeName: Metric
            Metric:
              Expression: sum(overdrive_state_time)
              Variables:
                - Name: overdrive_state_time
                  Value:
                    PropertyLogicalId: OverdriveStateTime
                    HierarchyLogicalId: TurbineHierarchy
              Window:
                Tumbling:

        - Name: Total Power

          DataType: DOUBLE
          Unit: kW
          Type:
            TypeName: Metric
            Metric:
              Expression: sum(average_power)
              Variables:
                - Name: average_power
                  Value:

                    HierarchyLogicalId: TurbineHierarchy

                Tumbling:

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: >-
  Prerequisite IAM role and custom AWS Systems Manager Automation documents
  used by AWS Config Conformance Pack remediation for PCI compliance controls.

Resources:
  PCIAutomationAssumeRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: !Sub 'pciautomationassumerole-${AWS::Region}'
      Description: Role assumed by AWS Systems Manager Automation for PCI compliance remediation.
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: AllowSSMEC2AndEventsToAssumeRole
            Effect: Allow
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
            Principal:
              Service:
                - ssm.amazonaws.com
                - ec2.amazonaws.com
                - events.amazonaws.com
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: PCIAutomationRemediationPolicy
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Sid: EC2RemediationPermissions
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - ec2:DescribeAddresses
                  - ec2:ReleaseAddress
                  - ec2:DescribeSecurityGroups
                  - ec2:DeleteSecurityGroup
                  - ec2:RevokeSecurityGroupIngress
                  - ec2:RevokeSecurityGroupEgress
                Resource: '*'
              - Sid: AutoScalingRemediationPermissions
                Effect: Allow
                Action: autoscaling:UpdateAutoScalingGroup
                Resource: '*'

  RestrictVPCDefaultSecurityGroup:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Document
    Properties:
      Name: RestrictVPCDefaultSecurityGroup
      DocumentType: Automation
      DocumentFormat: JSON
      Content:
        schemaVersion: '0.3'
        description: >-
          Revokes every ingress and egress rule from the default security
          group of a VPC, or from all default security groups when no VPC is
          supplied.
        assumeRole: '{{ AutomationAssumeRole }}'
        parameters:
          AutomationAssumeRole:
            type: String
            description: >-
              (Optional) The ARN of the IAM role that allows Automation to
              perform the actions on your behalf.
            default: ''
          VpcId:
            type: String
            description: >-
              (Optional) The ID of the VPC whose default security group is
              restricted. When omitted, all default security groups are
              restricted.
            default: ''
        mainSteps:
          - name: RevokeDefaultSecurityGroupRules
            action: aws:executeScript
            inputs:
              Runtime: python3.11
              Handler: handler
              InputPayload:
                VpcId: '{{ VpcId }}'
              Script: |-
                import boto3


                def handler(event, context):
                    vpc_id = (event or {}).get('VpcId', '') or ''
                    ec2 = boto3.client('ec2')

                    filters = [{'Name': 'group-name', 'Values': ['default']}]
                    if vpc_id:
                        filters.append({'Name': 'vpc-id', 'Values': [vpc_id]})

                    restricted = []
                    paginator = ec2.get_paginator('describe_security_groups')
                    for page in paginator.paginate(Filters=filters):
                        for group in page.get('SecurityGroups', []):
                            group_id = group['GroupId']
                            ingress = group.get('IpPermissions') or []
                            egress = group.get('IpPermissionsEgress') or []

                            if ingress:
                                ec2.revoke_security_group_ingress(
                                    GroupId=group_id,
                                    IpPermissions=ingress,
                                )
                            if egress:
                                ec2.revoke_security_group_egress(
                                    GroupId=group_id,
                                    IpPermissions=egress,
                                )
                            restricted.append(group_id)

                    return {'RestrictedSecurityGroups': restricted}

  DeleteUnusedSecurityGroups:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Document
    Properties:
      Name: DeleteUnusedSecurityGroups
      DocumentType: Automation
      DocumentFormat: JSON
      Content:
        schemaVersion: '0.3'
        description: >-
          Deletes security groups that are not attached to any network
          interface and are not referenced by any other security group.
        assumeRole: '{{ AutomationAssumeRole }}'
        parameters:
          AutomationAssumeRole:
            type: String
            description: >-
              (Optional) The ARN of the IAM role that allows Automation to
              perform the actions on your behalf.
            default: ''
        mainSteps:
          - name: DeleteUnusedSecurityGroups
            action: aws:executeScript
            inputs:
              Runtime: python3.11
              Handler: handler
              Script: |-
                import boto3


                def handler(event, context):
                    ec2 = boto3.client('ec2')

                    groups = []
                    paginator = ec2.get_paginator('describe_security_groups')
                    for page in paginator.paginate():
                        groups.extend(page.get('SecurityGroups', []))

                    referenced_group_ids = set()
                    for group in groups:
                        rules = (group.get('IpPermissions') or []) + (
                            group.get('IpPermissionsEgress') or []
                        )
                        for rule in rules:
                            for pair in rule.get('UserIdGroupPairs') or []:
                                if pair.get('GroupId'):
                                    referenced_group_ids.add(pair['GroupId'])

                    deleted = []
                    skipped = []
                    for group in groups:
                        group_id = group['GroupId']
                        group_name = group.get('GroupName', '')

                        if group_name == 'default':
                            skipped.append({'GroupId': group_id, 'Reason': 'default group'})
                            continue
                        if group.get('NetworkInterfaces'):
                            skipped.append({'GroupId': group_id, 'Reason': 'in use'})
                            continue
                        if group_id in referenced_group_ids:
                            skipped.append({'GroupId': group_id, 'Reason': 'referenced'})
                            continue

                        try:
                            ec2.delete_security_group(GroupId=group_id)
                            deleted.append(group_id)
                        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
                            skipped.append({'GroupId': group_id, 'Reason': str(exc)})

                    return {
                        'DeletedSecurityGroups': deleted,
                        'SkippedSecurityGroups': skipped,
                    }

  ReleaseUnassociatedElasticIPAddresses:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Document
    Properties:
      Name: ReleaseUnassociatedElasticIPAddresses
      DocumentType: Automation
      DocumentFormat: JSON
      Content:
        schemaVersion: '0.3'
        description: >-
          Releases all Elastic IP addresses that are not associated with an
          instance or network interface, using each address allocation ID.
        assumeRole: '{{ AutomationAssumeRole }}'
        parameters:
          AutomationAssumeRole:
            type: String
            description: >-
              (Optional) The ARN of the IAM role that allows Automation to
              perform the actions on your behalf.
            default: ''
        mainSteps:
          - name: ReleaseUnassociatedAddresses
            action: aws:executeScript
            inputs:
              Runtime: python3.11
              Handler: handler
              Script: |-
                import boto3


                def handler(event, context):
                    ec2 = boto3.client('ec2')
                    released = []
                    skipped = []

                    paginator = ec2.get_paginator('describe_addresses')
                    for page in paginator.paginate():
                        for address in page.get('Addresses', []):
                            allocation_id = address.get('AllocationId')
                            if not allocation_id:
                                skipped.append(
                                    {'PublicIp': address.get('PublicIp'), 'Reason': 'no allocation ID'}
                                )
                                continue
                            if address.get('AssociationId'):
                                skipped.append(
                                    {'AllocationId': allocation_id, 'Reason': 'associated'}
                                )
                                continue

                            ec2.release_address(AllocationId=allocation_id)
                            released.append(allocation_id)

                    return {
                        'ReleasedAllocationIds': released,
                        'SkippedAddresses': skipped,
                    }

  UpdateAutoScalingGroupHealthCheck:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Document
    Properties:

      Content:

                def handler(event, context):

                    autoscaling = boto3.client('autoscaling')
                    autoscaling.update_auto_scaling_group(

                        HealthCheckGracePeriod=300,
                    )

                    return {

                        'HealthCheckType': 'ELB',
                        'HealthCheckGracePeriod': 300,

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: "2010-09-09"
Description: >-
  Automation infrastructure for failing over an Aurora Global Database.
  The template creates IAM roles, a Systems Manager Automation document that
  evaluates Route 53 Application Recovery Controller routing controls, fails
  over the global cluster, flips the routing controls and stores the new
  writer endpoint in Secrets Manager, and a Lambda function that starts the
  automation.

Parameters:
  PrimaryRegion:
    Type: String
    Default: us-east-1
    Description: AWS Region that hosts the primary Aurora DB cluster.
  SecondaryRegion:
    Type: String
    Default: us-west-2
    Description: AWS Region that hosts the secondary Aurora DB cluster.
  GlobalClusterIdentifier:
    Type: String
    Default: aurora-global-database
    Description: Identifier of the Aurora global cluster to fail over.
  TargetDbClusterIdentifier:
    Type: String
    Default: aurora-global-database-secondary
    Description: Identifier of the secondary DB cluster that becomes the new writer.
  PrimaryRoutingControlArn:
    Type: String
    Default: ""
    Description: ARN of the ARC routing control in front of the primary Region.
  SecondaryRoutingControlArn:
    Type: String
    Default: ""
    Description: ARN of the ARC routing control in front of the secondary Region.

Resources:
  SsmAutomationRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      Description: Execution role used by the Aurora global database failover automation.
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: "2012-10-17"
        Statement:
          - Sid: AllowSystemsManagerAutomation
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: ssm.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: AuroraGlobalDatabaseFailoverPermissions
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: "2012-10-17"
            Statement:
              - Sid: AuroraGlobalDatabaseManagement
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - rds:DescribeGlobalClusters
                  - rds:DescribeDBClusters
                  - rds:DescribeDBClusterEndpoints
                  - rds:DescribeDBInstances
                  - rds:FailoverGlobalCluster
                  - rds:SwitchoverGlobalCluster
                  - rds:ListTagsForResource
                Resource: "*"
              - Sid: ArcRoutingControlManagement
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - route53-recovery-cluster:GetRoutingControlState
                  - route53-recovery-cluster:UpdateRoutingControlState
                  - route53-recovery-cluster:ListRoutingControls
                  - route53-recovery-control-config:DescribeCluster
                  - route53-recovery-control-config:DescribeControlPanel
                  - route53-recovery-control-config:DescribeRoutingControl
                  - route53-recovery-control-config:ListClusters
                  - route53-recovery-control-config:ListControlPanels
                  - route53-recovery-control-config:ListRoutingControls
                Resource: "*"
              - Sid: SecretsManagerWriterEndpoint
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - secretsmanager:DescribeSecret
                  - secretsmanager:GetSecretValue
                  - secretsmanager:PutSecretValue
                  - secretsmanager:UpdateSecret
                Resource: "*"
              - Sid: SystemsManagerAutomation
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - ssm:DescribeAutomationExecutions
                  - ssm:DescribeAutomationStepExecutions
                  - ssm:DescribeDocument
                  - ssm:GetAutomationExecution
                  - ssm:GetDocument
                  - ssm:ListDocuments
                  - ssm:StartAutomationExecution
                Resource: "*"

  LambdaExecutionRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      Description: Execution role for the Lambda function that triggers the failover automation.
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: "2012-10-17"
        Statement:
          - Sid: AllowLambdaService
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: lambda.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: TriggerFailoverAutomationPermissions
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: "2012-10-17"
            Statement:
              - Sid: StartAndMonitorAutomationExecutions
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - ssm:StartAutomationExecution
                  - ssm:GetAutomationExecution
                  - ssm:DescribeAutomationExecutions
                  - ssm:DescribeAutomationStepExecutions
                  - ssm:StopAutomationExecution
                Resource: "*"
              - Sid: PassAutomationExecutionRole
                Effect: Allow
                Action: iam:PassRole
                Resource: !GetAtt SsmAutomationRole.Arn
                Condition:
                  StringEquals:
                    iam:PassedToService: ssm.amazonaws.com
              - Sid: WriteLambdaLogs
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - logs:CreateLogGroup
                  - logs:CreateLogStream
                  - logs:PutLogEvents
                Resource: !Sub "arn:${AWS::Partition}:logs:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:log-group:/aws/lambda/TriggerFailover:*"

  FailoverStateSecret:
    Type: AWS::SecretsManager::Secret
    Properties:
      Description: Tracks the Aurora global database writer endpoint and the active Region.
      SecretString: !Sub '{"writer_endpoint":"","active_region":"${PrimaryRegion}"}'

  AuroraFailoverDocument:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Document
    Properties:
      Name: AuroraGlobalDatabaseFailoverSSMDocument
      DocumentType: Automation
      Content:
        schemaVersion: "0.3"
        description: Fail over an Aurora Global Database and update ARC routing controls.
        assumeRole: "{{ AutomationAssumeRole }}"
        parameters:
          PrimaryRegion:
            type: String
            default: us-east-1
            description: Region that hosts the primary Aurora DB cluster.
          SecondaryRegion:
            type: String
            description: Region that hosts the secondary Aurora DB cluster.
          GlobalClusterIdentifier:
            type: String
            description: Identifier of the Aurora global cluster.
          TargetDbClusterIdentifier:
            type: String
            description: DB cluster identifier in the secondary Region that becomes the writer.
          PrimaryRoutingControlArn:
            type: String
            description: ARN of the ARC routing control for the primary Region.
          SecondaryRoutingControlArn:
            type: String
            description: ARN of the ARC routing control for the secondary Region.
          SecretId:
            type: String
            description: ARN or name of the Secrets Manager secret that stores the writer endpoint.
          AutomationAssumeRole:
            type: String
            description: ARN of the IAM role that Automation assumes while running the steps.
        mainSteps:
          - name: DetermineActiveRegion
            action: aws:executeScript
            description: Determine the active Region by reading the ARC routing control states.
            inputs:
              Runtime: python3.11
              Handler: script_handler
              InputPayload:
                PrimaryRegion: "{{ PrimaryRegion }}"
                SecondaryRegion: "{{ SecondaryRegion }}"
                PrimaryRoutingControlArn: "{{ PrimaryRoutingControlArn }}"
                SecondaryRoutingControlArn: "{{ SecondaryRoutingControlArn }}"
              Script: |-
                import boto3


                def script_handler(events, context):
                    primary_arn = events["PrimaryRoutingControlArn"]
                    secondary_arn = events["SecondaryRoutingControlArn"]

                    primary_client = boto3.client(
                        "route53-recovery-cluster",
                        region_name=primary_arn.split(":")[3],
                    )
                    secondary_client = boto3.client(
                        "route53-recovery-cluster",
                        region_name=secondary_arn.split(":")[3],
                    )

                    primary_state = primary_client.get_routing_control_state(
                        RoutingControlArn=primary_arn
                    )["RoutingControlState"]
                    secondary_state = secondary_client.get_routing_control_state(
                        RoutingControlArn=secondary_arn
                    )["RoutingControlState"]

                    if primary_state == "On":
                        active_region = events["PrimaryRegion"]
                    elif secondary_state == "On":
                        active_region = events["SecondaryRegion"]
                    else:
                        raise RuntimeError(
                            "Neither ARC routing control is On; the active Region cannot be determined."
                        )

                    return {
                        "ActiveRegion": active_region,
                        "PrimaryState": primary_state,
                        "SecondaryState": secondary_state,
                    }
            outputs:
              - Name: ActiveRegion
                Selector: $.Payload.ActiveRegion
                Type: String
              - Name: PrimaryState
                Selector: $.Payload.PrimaryState
                Type: String
              - Name: SecondaryState
                Selector: $.Payload.SecondaryState
                Type: String

          - name: FailoverGlobalCluster
            action: aws:executeScript
            description: Promote the secondary Aurora DB cluster to the global cluster writer.
            inputs:
              Runtime: python3.11
              Handler: script_handler
              InputPayload:
                SecondaryRegion: "{{ SecondaryRegion }}"
                GlobalClusterIdentifier: "{{ GlobalClusterIdentifier }}"
                TargetDbClusterIdentifier: "{{ TargetDbClusterIdentifier }}"
              Script: |-
                import boto3


                def script_handler(events, context):
                    rds = boto3.client("rds", region_name=events["SecondaryRegion"])
                    rds.failover_global_cluster(
                        GlobalClusterIdentifier=events["GlobalClusterIdentifier"],
                        TargetDbClusterIdentifier=events["TargetDbClusterIdentifier"],
                    )

                    waiter = rds.get_waiter("db_cluster_available")
                    waiter.wait(
                        DBClusterIdentifier=events["TargetDbClusterIdentifier"],
                        WaiterConfig={"Delay": 15, "MaxAttempts": 40},
                    )

                    clusters = rds.describe_db_clusters(
                        DBClusterIdentifier=events["TargetDbClusterIdentifier"]
                    )["DBClusters"]

                    return {
                        "ActiveRegion": events["SecondaryRegion"],
                        "WriterEndpoint": clusters[0]["Endpoint"],
                    }
            outputs:
              - Name: ActiveRegion
                Selector: $.Payload.ActiveRegion
                Type: String
              - Name: WriterEndpoint
                Selector: $.Payload.WriterEndpoint
                Type: String

          - name: FlipRoutingControlsAndUpdateSecret
            action: aws:executeScript
            description: Flip the ARC routing controls and store the new writer endpoint.
            inputs:
              Runtime: python3.11
              Handler: script_handler
              InputPayload:
                ActiveRegion: "{{ DetermineActiveRegion.ActiveRegion }}"
                PrimaryRegion: "{{ PrimaryRegion }}"
                SecondaryRegion: "{{ SecondaryRegion }}"
                WriterEndpoint: "{{ FailoverGlobalCluster.WriterEndpoint }}"
                PrimaryRoutingControlArn: "{{ PrimaryRoutingControlArn }}"
                SecondaryRoutingControlArn: "{{ SecondaryRoutingControlArn }}"
                SecretId: "{{ SecretId }}"
              Script: |-
                import json

                import boto3


                def script_handler(events, context):
                    if events["ActiveRegion"] == events["SecondaryRegion"]:
                        turn_off_arn = events["PrimaryRoutingControlArn"]
                        turn_on_arn = events["SecondaryRoutingControlArn"]
                        primary_state = "Off"
                        secondary_state = "On"
                    else:
                        turn_off_arn = events["SecondaryRoutingControlArn"]
                        turn_on_arn = events["PrimaryRoutingControlArn"]
                        primary_state = "On"
                        secondary_state = "Off"

                    off_client = boto3.client(
                        "route53-recovery-cluster",
                        region_name=turn_off_arn.split(":")[3],
                    )
                    off_client.update_routing_control_state(
                        RoutingControlArn=turn_off_arn,
                        RoutingControlState="Off",
                    )

                    on_client = boto3.client(
                        "route53-recovery-cluster",
                        region_name=turn_on_arn.split(":")[3],
                    )
                    on_client.update_routing_control_state(
                        RoutingControlArn=turn_on_arn,
                        RoutingControlState="On",
                    )

                    secretsmanager = boto3.client(
                        "secretsmanager",
                        region_name=events["ActiveRegion"],
                    )
                    secretsmanager.put_secret_value(
                        SecretId=events["SecretId"],
                        SecretString=json.dumps(
                            {
                                "writer_endpoint": events["WriterEndpoint"],
                                "active_region": events["ActiveRegion"],
                            }
                        ),
                    )

                    return {
                        "ActiveRegion": events["ActiveRegion"],
                        "PrimaryState": primary_state,
                        "SecondaryState": secondary_state,
                        "WriterEndpoint": events["WriterEndpoint"],
                    }
            outputs:
              - Name: ActiveRegion
                Selector: $.Payload.ActiveRegion
                Type: String
              - Name: PrimaryState
                Selector: $.Payload.PrimaryState
                Type: String
              - Name: SecondaryState
                Selector: $.Payload.SecondaryState
                Type: String
              - Name: WriterEndpoint
                Selector: $.Payload.WriterEndpoint
                Type: String

  TriggerFailoverFunction:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    Properties:
      FunctionName: TriggerFailover
      Description: Starts the Aurora global database failover SSM automation and monitors it.
      Runtime: python3.13
      Handler: index.handler
      Role: !GetAtt LambdaExecutionRole.Arn
      MemorySize: 256
      Timeout: 900
      Environment:
        Variables:
          SSM_DOCUMENT_NAME: !Ref AuroraFailoverDocument
          PRIMARY_REGION: !Ref PrimaryRegion
          SECONDARY_REGION: !Ref SecondaryRegion
          GLOBAL_CLUSTER_IDENTIFIER: !Ref GlobalClusterIdentifier
          TARGET_DB_CLUSTER_IDENTIFIER: !Ref TargetDbClusterIdentifier
          PRIMARY_ROUTING_CONTROL_ARN: !Ref PrimaryRoutingControlArn
          SECONDARY_ROUTING_CONTROL_ARN: !Ref SecondaryRoutingControlArn
          WRITER_ENDPOINT_SECRET_ID: !Ref FailoverStateSecret
          AUTOMATION_ASSUME_ROLE_ARN: !GetAtt SsmAutomationRole.Arn
      Code:
        ZipFile: |
          import os
          import time

          import boto3

          ssm = boto3.client("ssm")

          POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS = 15
          MAX_WAIT_SECONDS = 840
          TERMINAL_STATES = {
              "Success",
              "Failed",
              "Cancelled",
              "TimedOut",
          }


          def _parameters():
              return {
                  "PrimaryRegion": [os.environ["PRIMARY_REGION"]],
                  "SecondaryRegion": [os.environ["SECONDARY_REGION"]],
                  "GlobalClusterIdentifier": [os.environ["GLOBAL_CLUSTER_IDENTIFIER"]],
                  "TargetDbClusterIdentifier": [os.environ["TARGET_DB_CLUSTER_IDENTIFIER"]],
                  "PrimaryRoutingControlArn": [os.environ["PRIMARY_ROUTING_CONTROL_ARN"]],
                  "SecondaryRoutingControlArn": [os.environ["SECONDARY_ROUTING_CONTROL_ARN"]],
                  "SecretId": [os.environ["WRITER_ENDPOINT_SECRET_ID"]],
                  "AutomationAssumeRole": [os.environ["AUTOMATION_ASSUME_ROLE_ARN"]],
              }


          def _wait_for_completion(execution_id):
              deadline = time.time() + MAX_WAIT_SECONDS
              status = "InProgress"
              while time.time() < deadline:
                  response = ssm.get_automation_execution(
                      AutomationExecutionId=execution_id
                  )
                  status = response["AutomationExecution"]["AutomationExecutionStatus"]
                  if status in TERMINAL_STATES:
                      break
                  time.sleep(POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS)
              return status


          def handler(event, context):
              execution = ssm.start_automation_execution(
                  DocumentName=os.environ["SSM_DOCUMENT_NAME"],
                  Parameters=_parameters(),
              )
              execution_id = execution["AutomationExecutionId"]
              status = _wait_for_completion(execution_id)
              return {
                  "automationExecutionId": execution_id,
                  "status": status,
              }

Description: >-
  Multi-tenant QuickSight dashboard application running on AWS App Runner.
  The template provisions a private ECR repository, builds and pushes the

Resources:

  AppImageRepository:

                Resource:
                  - !Sub 'arn:aws:codebuild:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:project/${BuildProject}'

  ImageBuildFunction:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    Properties:
      Description: Starts the image build and waits for it to finish
      Runtime: python3.12

      Role: !GetAtt ImageBuildFunctionRole.Arn
      Code:
        ZipFile: |
          import json
          import time
          import urllib.request

          import boto3

          codebuild = boto3.client("codebuild")


          def respond(event, context, status, physical_id=None, data=None, reason=""):
              body = json.dumps(
                  {
                      "Status": status,
                      "Reason": reason
                      or "See CloudWatch Logs: %s" % context.log_group_name,
                      "PhysicalResourceId": physical_id
                      or event.get("PhysicalResourceId")
                      or context.log_stream_name,
                      "StackId": event["StackId"],
                      "RequestId": event["RequestId"],
                      "LogicalResourceId": event["LogicalResourceId"],
                      "Data": data or {},
                  }
              ).encode("utf-8")
              request = urllib.request.Request(
                  event["ResponseURL"],
                  data=body,
                  method="PUT",
                  headers={"Content-Type": ""},
              )
              urllib.request.urlopen(request)


          def wait_for_build(build_id, timeout_seconds):
              deadline = time.time() + timeout_seconds
              while time.time() < deadline:
                  time.sleep(15)
                  builds = codebuild.batch_get_builds(ids=[build_id]).get("builds", [])
                  if not builds:
                      continue
                  status = builds[0].get("buildStatus")
                  if status == "SUCCEEDED":
                      return True, status
                  if status in ("FAILED", "FAULT", "STOPPED", "TIMED_OUT"):
                      return False, status
              return False, "TIMED_OUT_LOCAL"


          def handler(event, context):
              try:
                  if event["RequestType"] == "Delete":
                      respond(
                          event,
                          context,
                          "SUCCESS",
                          physical_id=event.get("PhysicalResourceId"),
                      )
                      return
                  project_name = event["ResourceProperties"]["ProjectName"]
                  build_id = codebuild.start_build(projectName=project_name)["build"]["id"]
                  ok, status = wait_for_build(build_id, 780)
                  if ok:
                      respond(
                          event,
                          context,
                          "SUCCESS",
                          physical_id=build_id,
                          data={"BuildId": build_id, "BuildStatus": status},
                      )
                  else:
                      respond(
                          event,
                          context,
                          "FAILED",
                          physical_id=build_id,
                          reason="Container image build did not succeed: %s" % status,
                      )
              except Exception as error:
                  respond(event, context, "FAILED", reason=str(error))

  ImageBuild:

    Properties:
      ServiceToken: !GetAtt ImageBuildFunction.Arn

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: >-
  CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark aligned VPC Flow Logs remediation built on AWS
  Systems Manager Automation. The template creates a CloudWatch Logs log group
  with long-lived retention for flow log data, a role that VPC Flow Logs and the
  automation assume to publish flow records and manage EC2 flow log resources, a
  separate automation execution role with the permissions required to run the
  automation steps, a remediation automation document that enables REJECT
  traffic flow logging on a supplied VPC, and a dependent automation document
  that routes the same remediation through AWS Systems Manager Change Manager as
  a formal change request.

Resources:

  FlowLogsLogGroup:
    Type: AWS::Logs::LogGroup
    Properties:
      LogGroupName: !Sub '/aws/vpc-flow-logs/${AWS::StackName}'
      RetentionInDays: 2557

  FlowLogsRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      Description: >-
        Assumed by VPC Flow Logs to write flow records to the flow log group and
        by AWS Systems Manager Automation to manage EC2 flow log resources.
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: AllowVpcFlowLogsService
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service:
                - vpc-flow-logs.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
          - Sid: AllowAutomationService
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service:
                - ssm.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: FlowLogsLogGroupWriteAccess
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Sid: WriteFlowLogRecords
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - logs:CreateLogStream
                  - logs:PutLogEvents
                  - logs:DescribeLogStreams
                Resource:
                  - !GetAtt FlowLogsLogGroup.Arn
                  - !Sub '${FlowLogsLogGroup.Arn}:*'
              - Sid: DescribeFlowLogsLogGroups
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - logs:DescribeLogGroups
                Resource: '*'
        - PolicyName: FlowLogResourceManagement
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Sid: ManageVpcFlowLogs
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - ec2:CreateFlowLogs
                  - ec2:DescribeFlowLogs
                  - ec2:DeleteFlowLogs
                  - ec2:DescribeVpcs
                  - ec2:DescribeSubnets
                  - ec2:DescribeNetworkInterfaces
                  - ec2:DescribeTags
                Resource: '*'

  FlowLogsRolePassRolePolicy:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Policy
    Properties:
      PolicyName: PassFlowLogsRoleToVpcFlowLogs
      Roles:
        - !Ref FlowLogsRole
      PolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: PassFlowLogsRoleToFlowLogs
            Effect: Allow
            Action: iam:PassRole
            Resource: !GetAtt FlowLogsRole.Arn
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                iam:PassedToService: vpc-flow-logs.amazonaws.com

  AutomationExecutionRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      Description: >-
        Execution role assumed by AWS Systems Manager Automation to run the VPC
        flow log remediation steps and to start Change Manager change requests.
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: AllowAutomationService
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service:
                - ssm.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: VpcFlowLogsRemediationAccess
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Sid: ManageVpcFlowLogs
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - ec2:CreateFlowLogs
                  - ec2:DeleteFlowLogs
                  - ec2:DescribeFlowLogs
                  - ec2:DescribeVpcs
                  - ec2:DescribeSubnets
                  - ec2:DescribeNetworkInterfaces
                  - ec2:DescribeTags
                Resource: '*'
              - Sid: ManageFlowLogsLogGroup
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - logs:CreateLogGroup
                  - logs:CreateLogStream
                  - logs:PutLogEvents
                  - logs:DescribeLogGroups
                  - logs:DescribeLogStreams
                  - logs:PutRetentionPolicy
                Resource: '*'
              - Sid: ManageAutomationAndChangeRequests
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - ssm:StartChangeRequestExecution
                  - ssm:GetAutomationExecution
                  - ssm:DescribeAutomationExecutions
                  - ssm:DescribeAutomationStepExecutions
                  - ssm:GetDocument
                  - ssm:DescribeDocument
                  - ssm:ListDocuments
                  - ssm:ListDocumentVersions
                  - ssm:SendAutomationSignal
                  - ssm:StopAutomationExecution
                Resource: '*'
              - Sid: PassFlowLogsRoleToFlowLogs
                Effect: Allow
                Action: iam:PassRole
                Resource: !GetAtt FlowLogsRole.Arn
                Condition:
                  StringEquals:
                    iam:PassedToService: vpc-flow-logs.amazonaws.com

  EnableVpcFlowLogsDocument:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Document
    Properties:
      DocumentType: Automation
      Content:
        schemaVersion: '0.3'
        description: >-
          Enables VPC Flow Logs with REJECT traffic capture on a supplied VPC so
          that the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark control for VPC flow logging is
          satisfied. The flow records are delivered to the stack managed
          CloudWatch Logs log group using the VPC Flow Logs role.
        assumeRole: !GetAtt AutomationExecutionRole.Arn
        parameters:
          VpcId:
            type: String
            description: The ID of the VPC on which to enable flow logging.
          LogGroupName:
            type: String
            default: !Ref FlowLogsLogGroup
            description: The CloudWatch Logs log group that receives flow records.
          FlowLogsRoleArn:
            type: String
            default: !GetAtt FlowLogsRole.Arn
            description: The role that VPC Flow Logs assumes to publish flow records.
        mainSteps:
          - name: EnableVpcFlowLogs
            action: aws:executeScript
            description: >-
              Calls the Amazon EC2 CreateFlowLogs API from a Python script to
              enable REJECT traffic flow logging for the requested VPC.
            inputs:
              Runtime: python3.11
              Handler: enable_vpc_flow_logs
              InputPayload:
                VpcId: '{{ VpcId }}'
                LogGroupName: '{{ LogGroupName }}'
                FlowLogsRoleArn: '{{ FlowLogsRoleArn }}'
              Script: |-
                import boto3


                def enable_vpc_flow_logs(events, context):
                    vpc_id = events['VpcId']
                    log_group_name = events['LogGroupName']
                    flow_logs_role_arn = events['FlowLogsRoleArn']

                    ec2 = boto3.client('ec2')

                    existing_flow_logs = ec2.describe_flow_logs(
                        Filters=[{'Name': 'resource-id', 'Values': [vpc_id]}]
                    ).get('FlowLogs', [])

                    matching_flow_logs = [
                        flow_log
                        for flow_log in existing_flow_logs
                        if flow_log.get('LogDestinationType') == 'cloud-watch-logs'
                        and flow_log.get('TrafficType') == 'REJECT'
                        and flow_log.get('LogGroupName') == log_group_name
                    ]
                    if matching_flow_logs:
                        flow_log_ids = [
                            flow_log['FlowLogId'] for flow_log in matching_flow_logs
                        ]
                        return {
                            'FlowLogIds': flow_log_ids,
                            'Message': (
                                'A matching REJECT traffic flow log already exists '
                                'for {0}.'.format(vpc_id)
                            ),
                        }

                    response = ec2.create_flow_logs(
                        DeliverLogsPermissionArn=flow_logs_role_arn,
                        LogGroupName=log_group_name,
                        ResourceIds=[vpc_id],
                        ResourceType='VPC',
                        TrafficType='REJECT',
                        LogDestinationType='cloud-watch-logs',
                    )

                    unsuccessful = response.get('Unsuccessful', [])
                    if unsuccessful:
                        raise RuntimeError(
                            'Unable to enable flow logging for {0}: {1}'.format(
                                vpc_id, unsuccessful
                            )
                        )

                    flow_log_ids = response.get('FlowLogIds', [])
                    if not flow_log_ids:
                        raise RuntimeError(
                            'CreateFlowLogs returned no flow log IDs for {0}.'.format(
                                vpc_id
                            )
                        )

                    return {
                        'FlowLogIds': flow_log_ids,
                        'Message': (
                            'Enabled REJECT traffic flow logging for {0}.'.format(
                                vpc_id
                            )
                        ),
                    }
            outputs:
              - Name: FlowLogIds
                Type: StringList
                Selector: $.Payload.FlowLogIds
              - Name: Message
                Type: String
                Selector: $.Payload.Message

  EnableVpcFlowLogsWithChangeManagerDocument:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Document
    Properties:
      DocumentType: Automation
      Content:
        schemaVersion: '0.3'
        description: >-
          Routes the CIS VPC flow log remediation through AWS Systems Manager
          Change Manager as a formal change request. The change request runs the
          EnableVpcFlowLogs remediation document so that real-world use of the
          fix is recorded and approved through Change Manager.
        assumeRole: !GetAtt AutomationExecutionRole.Arn
        parameters:
          VpcId:
            type: String
            description: The ID of the VPC on which to enable flow logging.
          RemediationDocumentName:
            type: String
            default: !Ref EnableVpcFlowLogsDocument
            description: The remediation automation document to run as a runbook.
          ChangeTemplateDocumentName:
            type: String
            default: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-VpcFlowLogsChangeTemplate'
            description: >-
              The Change Manager change template document that defines the
              approval workflow for the flow log remediation change request.
          LogGroupName:
            type: String
            default: !Ref FlowLogsLogGroup
            description: The CloudWatch Logs log group that receives flow records.
          FlowLogsRoleArn:
            type: String
            default: !GetAtt FlowLogsRole.Arn
            description: The role that VPC Flow Logs assumes to publish flow records.
          ChangeRequestName:
            type: String
            default: !Sub 'EnableVpcFlowLogs-${AWS::StackName}'
            description: A name that identifies the Change Manager change request.
        mainSteps:
          - name: StartChangeRequestExecution
            action: aws:executeScript
            description: >-
              Calls the AWS Systems Manager StartChangeRequestExecution API from a
              Python script to create a formal change request whose runbook is the
              VPC flow log remediation document.
            inputs:
              Runtime: python3.11
              Handler: start_change_request

Description: Creates a reusable Route53 delegation set managed by a Lambda-backed custom resource.

Parameters:

    Default: ReusableDelegationSet
    Description: Name of the Lambda function that manages the delegation set.

Resources:

    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:

        Version: '2012-10-17'

          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - route53:CreateReusableDelegationSet
                  - route53:DeleteReusableDelegationSet

                  - route53:ListReusableDelegationSets
                Resource: '*'
